The study of isotones near N = 40 suggested a complex interplay between shell-model and deformation properties, with the nickel nucleus displaying a notable structural shift.

Researchers have introduced an innovative technique for accurately measuring the masses of extremely short-lived, unusual atomic isotopes over a wide range of frequencies. This method utilizes the principle of isochronous mass spectrometry, combining real-time ion velocity and trajectory analysis at the Lanzhou CSRe particle storage facility. Dubbed Bρ-defined isochronous mass spectrometry, or Bρ-IMS, this technique enhances precision and sensitivity, paving the way for new mass measurements. Specifically, in a single test setting, precise mass readings were obtained for $^{46}$Cr, $^{50}$Fe, and $^{54}$Ni with exceptionally low margins of error. This breakthrough technique will serve as a crucial tool for evaluating the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa quark interaction matrix and for further refining the measurements of highly rare, shortest-lived atomic isotopes.

This tutorial notebook exemplifies a novel technique for generating Boltzmann distributions of lattice field theories through normalizing flows, a subset of machine learning models. The underlying concepts presented in this tutorial are further elaborated upon in a companion paper (arXiv.2103.11199). The tutorial demonstrates its principles through simulations of a double-well potential and 1D Ising model, with additional examples including SU(2) Yang-Mills theory and (2+1)-d compact QCD.

We aim to enhance the accuracy of structured text recognition by incorporating predefined formats defined through regular expressions, thereby facilitating the identification of specific patterns. Our method, involving a Weighted Finite-State Transducer model, boosts recognition accuracy on targeted formats, with minimal losses in other instances. A key parameter governs the intensity of the formatting influence. The proposed technique finds applications in text analysis, particularly when dealing with formatted documents, domain-specific lexicons, or known formats like driver's license numbers and medicinal prescription terminology. We evaluate the effectiveness of this approach on a range of structured text datasets and examine its implications on overall recognition performance.

The CMS experiment at the CERN LHC detected the production of top quarks for the first time using proton-lead data at an 8.16 TeV nucleon-nucleon center-of-mass energy. Top quark production was identified in events featuring one isolated electron or muon and four or more jets, from a data set totaling 174 inverse nanobarns of luminosity. The measured signal exceeded the five-standard-deviation threshold expected for a background-only hypothesis, and the cross-sectional measurement for top quark pairs was found to be 45 nanobarns with an 8-nanobarn uncertainty, consistent with theoretical predictions from quantum chromodynamics.

This study focuses on key elements in cross-domain text-to-SQL parsing, specifically schema linking and value filling. To enhance encoding abilities, a column selection auxiliary task is proposed, leveraging explicit targets for relevance matching. Additionally, two value filling approaches are presented to bridge the gap between current zero-shot parsers and practical applications, considering that many existing parsers overlook value filling in synthesized SQL. Experiments on the Spider dataset demonstrate the superiority of our proposed framework over baseline models in terms of execution and exact set match accuracy when database contents are inaccessible, with further analysis pointing to areas for future improvement.

The ongoing LoTSS survey is conducting a thorough observation of the Northern sky to better understand how the large-scale structure of the Universe changes and develops. Although only 1% of the sky is covered in the LoTSS DR1 data release, analysis shows fluctuations that need to be understood. To address these issues, mock catalogues are created to predict potential sources of error and galaxy clustering patterns in the LoTSS data are studied. The study also employs an advanced analysis technique to find the most accurate galaxy distribution and multiple object classification for the LoTSS data based on possible galaxy evolutionary stages. After eliminating areas of noisy data, the LoTSS data is divided into different density levels and galaxy distribution patterns, multicolour classification for the LoTSS data are studied. The LoTSS data is also compared with other surveys such as SDSS and VSA to find consistent results across different observations.

The High-Dimensional Rank Lasso (HDR Lasso) model offers a computationally efficient solution to handle complex data analysis. Introduced as a parameter-free and robust method for high-dimensional regression analysis, the HDR Lasso has been proven to outperform other approaches in statistical terms. Mathematically, the HDR Lasso is equivalent to an optimization problem with an L1-regularized loss function that utilizes Jaeckel's dispersion function and Wilcoxon scores, making traditional lasso algorithms ineffective due to nondifferentiability. Building on the adaptive sieving strategy from the Exclusive Lasso problem, we introduce a novel HDR Lasso solution that takes full advantage of the problem's sparse nature, solving smaller subproblems in each iteration through the proximal point algorithm, which leverages the problem's nonsmooth terms effectively. Our extensive numerical experiments validate the proposed Adaptive-Sieving Proximal Point Algorithm's robustness across various noise types, as well as its high efficiency, particularly for large-dimensional features, when compared to alternative methods.

Identifying whether an optimal solution is localized or universal is particularly challenging in complex optimization problems. This work addresses that challenge by demonstrating the existence of a single, optimal, and universal method for achieving the lowest possible rate of entropy production in non-equilibrium thermal machines. This optimal approach remains unchanged over time and has a continuously varying rate. A fundamental functional, linked to the rate of entropy production, is proven to be convex in relation to the system's state. This breakthrough enables us to reliably determine the optimal final state and rate of entropy production, and importantly, reveals that the optimal path does not diverge from these outcomes. This means we can safely apply convex optimization techniques to the function and safely apply the principle of linear programming to achieve the optimal solution. This universal method is solely based on the system's configuration and is independent of the control parameters and history of the process. This discovery is significant for efficiently operating small thermal machines and understanding how to properly and efficiently manage the control of these devices.

Over the past decade, significant advancements in artificial intelligence have positioned it as a key tool for addressing environmental concerns, primarily reducing greenhouse gas emissions. However, researchers have lately come to recognize that increasingly complex AI models require substantial amounts of energy to train and typically necessitate the construction of specialized hardware, which contributes to environmental degradation. To date, there has been limited examination of the environmental implications of using AI for environmental purposes. In this study, we provide an in-depth analysis of the environmental effects of AI-driven solutions aimed at mitigating climate change. These aspects include the carbon footprint generated during the production, usage, and disposal of AI hardware and software. Additionally, we highlight emerging concerns, provide practical solutions, and explore potential future research directions in this domain, including the need for increased transparency and accountability throughout AI development processes.

This paper investigates and classifies various prescriptive process monitoring methods, which identify potential issues during business processes and provide interventions to prevent problems at the point of execution. The systematic review encompasses a comprehensive analysis of the current approaches in the field. To better understand these methods, a conceptual framework has been developed to evaluate prescriptive process monitoring techniques based on performance targets, metrics, and intervention scopes. The findings of the study include a map of existing methods and a roadmap for future developments in this area, along with limitations and potential research avenues identified in the associated tool.

This study introduces an error control strategy for a Boussinesq model with adaptive coefficients, where temperature-dependent properties of heat transfer and fluid viscosity are taken into account. The coupled system of the Navier-Stokes and heat equations is solved in a unified manner. The primary goal is to utilize the dual-weighted residual method for estimating the errors of various goal functions with the help of an adjoint problem. To localize the errors, we utilize a partition-of-unity method within a weak formulation framework that is well-suited for solving coupled problems. This approach enables the implementation of adaptive algorithms that are validated by a range of numerical experiments, including one benchmark problem and two further investigations inspired by laser material processing. The efficiency and robustness of the developed framework are confirmed by the observed reductions in errors and effectivity indices.

Polynomial-time reduction methods, referred to as kernelization algorithms, decrease the size of problems within a predetermined limit. Specifically, the 'd-Set Matching' problem for integers 'd greater than 2', involves identifying a set with 'at least k' matching elements within a hypergraph. Researchers have shown, through the works of Bodlaender et al. [JCSS 2009], Fortnow and Santhanam [JCSS 2019], and Dell and Van Melkebeek [JACM 2014], a framework that can prove lower bounds on kernel size under specific hypotheses involving 'coNP is not in NP/poly'.  Our research provides the tightest lower bounds yet, proving it impossible to have a d-Set Matching kernel of size 'O(k^d minus {epsilon}) edges', except if a particular hypothesis fails. Furthermore, using reduction methods, we obtain lower bounds of 'O(k^d minus one minus {epsilon}) edges' for problems of finding 'k' sets of size 'd', each containing'vertex-disjoint cliques'.  Our research provides the tightest lower bounds yet, proving it impossible to have a d-Set Matching kernel of size 'O(k^d minus {epsilon}) edges', except if a particular hypothesis fails. Furthermore, using reduction methods, we obtain lower bounds of 'O(k^d minus one minus {epsilon}) edges' for problems of finding 'k' sets of size 'd

This study explores how opinions are shaped and social connections evolve in a complex system, governed by a delicate balance between friendly and hostile relationships. We have developed a model that captures how individuals with limited confidence in their judgments form opinions based on their personal relationships. We considered scenarios with one and two distinct aspects of opinions, and found that our framework consistently leads to the separation of agents into two distinct groups, characterized by distinct opinion sets. Depending on the level of trust, these groups either develop uniform views or multiple distinct perspectives within each group emerge. In the case of opinions based on a single dimension, the two groups have opposing views, forming a 'left' and 'right' category. In scenarios with multiple dimensions, the two groups are separated by a dividing line in opinion space. We have demonstrated that our results can partially explain a phenomenon previously observed by other researchers. Our work has implications for understanding how political ideologies become fragmented and how new parties might emerge.

We've investigated a newly constructed series of asymptotically flat, electrically charged black holes that form scalar "hair" when their charge increases at a fixed mass. Inside the event horizon, these black holes resemble a holographic superconducting material, exhibiting similar behavior in their scalar fields and culminating in a singularity that heavily depends on the black holes' parameters. Additionally, we've studied the stability of these black holes and found that certain modes become unstable as the charge approaches a critical value. Our findings also reveal how the scalar "hair" on these black holes influences their thermal properties and entropy.

Different genes exhibiting similar activation patterns may show distinct mRNA expression levels at different time points due to variations in transcription duration, RNA breakdown speed, and processing rates. The impact of RNA splicing on delaying mRNA production cannot be ignored. We developed a model combining transcription dynamics and RNA accumulation to estimate the rates of transcription, RNA production lag, and RNA breakdown using sequencing data from multiple time points. The model blends a mechanistic approach with a flexible statistical method, incorporating uncertainty into the calculations through Bayesian estimation. We applied this model to ER-alpha activated cells from a breast cancer line, analyzing transcription using ChIP-Seq data and mature RNA quantities from mRNA-Seq data. The results show that a considerable number of genes exhibit a prolonged period between transcription completion and mature RNA availability. Furthermore, genes exhibiting longer delays are typically shorter and are associated with retained introns in pre-mRNA data, suggesting significant production delays attributed to splicing events.

Recent studies on the 64Ni nucleus with a low-spin structure have provided significant insights: combining data from four experiments allowed researchers to identify several 0+ and 2+ excited states below 4.5 MeV, and characterize their properties. Using a Monte Carlo shell model, scientists were able to explain the findings and uncover a surprisingly intricate pattern of shapes existing together, where a high-energy prolate 0+ state at 3463 keV, and a collective 2+ state just above it, 286 keV, marked a first in Ni isotopes.

Chiral SU(N) gauge theories, consisting of Weyl fermions and additional fermions, are examined to analyze their dynamics. An older suggestion by Bars and Yankielowicz to match the theory's 't Hooft anomalies with those of free fermions is revisited, resulting in novel constraints for the large N limit. Furthermore, SU(N) theories with an additional Weyl fermion are studied, demonstrating a matching of 21 't Hooft anomalies with a Spin(8) gauge theory. This discovery hints at a non-supersymmetric expansion of the Pouliot and Strassler duality, while non-supersymmetric dualities involving vector-like matter in SO(N) and Sp(N) gauge theories, subject to Weingarten inequalities, are also explored.

A linear complementary pair of group codes $(C, D)$ is formed when the direct sum of $C$ and $D$ results in the entire group algebra $R[G]$, given a finite principal ideal ring $R$ and a finite group $G$. We identify a required and confirming criterion for pairs of group codes $(C, D)$ in group algebra $R[G]$ to be a linear complementary pair, subsequently proving the equivalence in terms of permutations between codes $C$ and the dual code $D^{\perp}$.

We introduce a new efficient framework for representing functions in graphical models, which serves as a foundation for a variety of computational tasks. Our concise model then leverages this framework, specifically using deterministic finite state automata within a variable elimination approach known as Bucket Elimination. We dub this variant FABE, which we found significantly enhances Bucket Elimination by substantially reducing the computational time and memory usage. Our FABE approach compares favourably to the current state of the art methods, particularly recursive best-first and structured message passing for the most probable explanation, as well as CPLEX, GUROBI and toulbar2 for constrained optimisation, by achieving a 5 orders of magnitude improvement in our experiments following a widely established evaluation procedure.

The visual appearance and auditory qualities of an object provide dual insights into its material properties.  In everyday situations, information from vision and hearing arrive simultaneously, but the integration of asynchronous cues is essential, as seen when we locate an object dropped on the ground after hearing its fall.  In this paper, a controlled environment for studying 3D object localization in real-time is established, involving an embodied robotic agent, a camera, and a microphone that identify a dropped object in a room.  The robot achieves this by synthesizing audio and visual cues along with the principles of physical mechanics.  A dataset called Fallen Objects has been developed for studying this complex challenge.  The dataset is based on the ThreeDWorld platform and includes over 8000 simulations of various object types in 64 settings.  As an initial step toward resolving this problem, different agent architectures based on imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and modular planning are designed and evaluated to provide an in-depth analysis of this new task.

When subjected to high stresses, the vast majority of dense mixtures undergo a sudden and extreme thickening, characterized by a transition from fluid-like behavior to rigidity. Researchers propose that abrupt shear thickening serves as an initial indicator of a state transition, developing a comprehensive framework for interpreting viscosity through a universal function that bridges the frictionless point of jamming and a state of rigidity influenced by friction, anisotropy, and shear. Studies involving cornstarch in glycerol and silica spheres in glycerol found that for these two systems, viscosity can be condensed into a singular, stress- and volume fraction-independent curve, revealing distinct scaling regimes that reflect different universality classes and implying that isotropic and anisotropic shear jamming have unique characteristics. Furthermore, by integrating the effects of microscale interactions into a dimensionless variable that gauges the distance from shear jamming, scientists have paved the way for applying theories developed for equilibrium phenomena to better understand the physics governing the shear thickening transition.

This study investigates the fluctuating electricity consumption in Ghana's period of power shortages by applying Markov switching models, namely MS-AR and AR. The data, comprising hourly electricity usage from January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014 provided by the Ghana Grid company, helped determine the best-fitting model as MS(2)-AR(4) based on different evaluation criteria. The parameters of this model were then estimated using an expectation-maximization algorithm, indicating that the likelihood of experiencing low electricity consumption is 87%, with the low consumption period expected to last approximately 7.8 hours a day. The model outperformed traditional AR models by effectively modeling peak and varied consumption patterns and identifying distinct regime changes during the day.

An area where Web search personalisation's effect on professional work has been inadequately studied is that of professional work done on the Web. This study examines how Web search personalisation impacts lawyers' task completion and decision-making when performing a critical task. We discovered that the way searches are personalised can lead to the omission of as much as 13% of relevant information, as found in our previous research. Lawyers' task completion and decision-making processes were observed and recorded, and their Web searches were analyzed. We identified instances where personalisation caused lawyers to miss important information, and calculated the minimum percentage of relevant information that could be missed due to personalisation. We found that personalisation affected lawyers' task completion and decision-making, and in some cases, resulted in incorrect decisions. These results imply that Web search personalisation could be problematic for professionals who use it to make important decisions.

Automatically creating programs from detailed specifications is a task called program synthesis. A novel framework for generating code based on flow charts is presented, where a deep neural network called GRCNN is trained to accurately interpret these visual specifications by identifying their semantic connections. By being trained end-to-end, GRCNN is capable of learning the significant relationships between program inputs, outputs, and control flow patterns, resulting in significantly improved accuracy rates. Specifically, our system is able to correctly interpret over 82% of the training examples and over 75% of the challenges in the Industrial dataset, while also outperforming existing methods by over 110% in the OpenSource dataset. A fully functioning version of this framework is available at https://synthesis.cs.cmu.edu/grcnn/.

This text explores multiple reduction techniques that facilitate the connection of Earth's climate models of varying complexity, emphasizing approaches that enable thorough reduction. It distills key mathematical concepts behind each method while showcasing several benchmark climate modeling examples for illustrative purposes.

The groundbreaking discovery of gravitational waves emanating from a binary neutron star merger in August 2017 paved the way for a new era in the field of multi-messenger astronomy. Kilonovae, produced by the expelled material from neutron star collisions, present an attractive opportunity for optical and near-infrared follow-up observations following the detection of GWs. The observation of the kilonova from GW 1780817 revealed crucial evidence for the astrophysical site of heavy element formation via the rapid neutron capture process or r-process. Given that properties of the emission are heavily influenced by the opacities of the expelled material, recent calls for enhancement in the limited available r-process atomic data have led to an increased need for precise atomic structure information. Consequently, this research aims to alleviate the present limitations in atomic structure data, focusing specifically on the Os-like isoelectronic sequence for low-charge states. Utilizing the relativistic atomic structure packages (GRASP0 and GRASP2K), the research obtained the necessary data, which included energy levels, E1, and M1 transition probabilities, along with line lists and expansion opacities for a diverse range of r-process elements. In particular, this research centered on the Os isoelectronic sequence, encompassing Os I, Ir II, Pt III, Au IV, and Hg V, with the obtained data benchmarked against existing experimental data and prior calculations. Furthermore, this research predicted emission spectra relevant to kilonovae,

Radiation oncologists' goal is to target tumors accurately while shielding surrounding vital organs, specifically the stomach and intestines, from x-ray beams. The incorporation of MR-Linac systems allows real-time tumor positioning, enabling precise radiation dosage adjustments based on shifting cell populations. The manual process of identifying these organs and calibrating X-ray beams can be lengthy, extending treatment times up to one hour a day, making automated techniques with deep learning essential. A recent paper explores the use of deep learning-based automation to streamline this complex task and provide faster access to treatment for a greater number of patients.

Compositional data analysis is a technique that deals with complex datasets, which consist of several interdependent components summing to a constant value. Common constant values are 1 and 100%. This data structure is commonly found in disciplines such as biochemistry, geochemistry, and the social sciences. Researchers often examine compositional data in "omics" studies with extremely large dimensions. The method involves calculating logratios – the logarithmic expressions of component proportions. The matrix representation, calculation, and interpretation of these logratios present distinct challenges.

The exoplanet sample from CORALIE/HARPS (Mayor et al., 2011), which was discovered through Doppler radial velocity measurements, does not demonstrate the anticipated 'desert' at high masses (10-$100 M_\odot) with close orbital radii (<=3 AU), as predicted by the runaway gas accretion theory. Notably, similar findings have emerged from the MOA gravitational microlensing survey, which did not detect the 'desert' effect for planets in slightly longer-period orbits with lower-mass host stars (Suzuki et al., 2018). These studies collectively suggest that runaway accretion is unlikely a dominant process in shaping the final mass and orbital characteristics of exoplanets according to core accretion theory.

Artificial intelligence models, modeled after biological agents, can regulate their awareness by restricting their input data to minimize information overload. A key challenge in developing such a system lies in allocating limited attention among various information sources for an agent to function efficiently. A new method presented in this study enables an artificial agent to manage its attention by taking small-scale observations of its surroundings. This approach involves the agent using a probabilistic model to estimate its likelihood of meeting task requirements through means of observable environmental changes. By leveraging this estimation, the agent can adjust its attention according to the expected reward it can gain by processing uncertain environmental observations. A straightforward yet powerful search algorithm is used to find the optimal attention allocation, and experimental validation is provided by simulating a range of scenarios, including a complex real-world example of a marine ecologist searching for species data.

Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) can efficiently solve complex problems that demand memory, error correction, and selection capabilities, mirroring brain circuit behaviors, albeit with limited applicability due to large training demands and memory needs. Brain structures pose constraints such as synaptic distance costs and thus inspired local masking, allowing task-independent predetermined graphs, even with sparsity rates as low as 4\%. We introduce locality-masked RNNs and make several breakthroughs, demonstrating these models match or outperform traditional fully-connected RNNs without manual network construction, can learn and adapt faster while reducing the data required to perform cognitive tasks efficiently. Additionally, we developed Mod-Cog, a comprehensive set of cognitive tasks which expands on existing benchmarks with significantly increased complexity, showcasing the efficacy of locality-masked RNNs to effectively solve both basic and sophisticated tasks within a broad task space.

We categorize nilpotent algebras by dimension with a focus on their commutative, commutative nilpotent and anticommutative properties. Our findings reveal the irreducibility of corresponding geometric spaces, allowing us to accurately calculate their dimensions and establish general families of algebras associated with each space. Additionally, we demonstrate how these results contribute to an understanding of the length of anticommutative algebras in further study.

Active galactic nuclei with exceptionally powerful radio signals are among the brightest known celestial sources, spanning across a wide range of wavelengths. These powerful jets from supermassive black holes can significantly influence the growth of the black hole itself, as well as its host galaxy. In the radio spectrum, these jets can be observed on various scales, but their X-ray and gamma-ray emissions are predicted to be concentrated on smaller scales, typically under 10 parsecs. Recent findings by the Chandra X-ray telescope have revealed the presence of kiloparsec-scale jets, which has sparked debate about the source of their high-energy radiation. This research aims to understand the high-energy emissions of kiloparsec-scale jets by investigating the connection between the magnetic fields that drive the jets and the electrons that inhabit the jets or their surroundings. By assuming that the high-energy electrons in the jets themselves are responsible for the observed emissions, our study can place constraints on the magnetic fields that maintain these complex astronomical features.

We perform a covariant expansion of the Einstein-Hilbert action in powers of
$1/c^2$, considering a generic spacetime foliation defined by $c$, the speed
of light. We achieve this through the application of a suitable 'pre-non-
relativistic' geometrical parametrization, thereby facilitating an
analytical $1/c^2$ expansion of general relativity. Ultimately, this method
permits an in-depth examination of the Einstein-Hilbert action expansion up to
its next-to-next-to-leading order.

This study presents an enhanced approach to 3D image features that incorporates invariance to discrete symmetry by considering inversions of spatial axes and image contrast.  The proposed framework includes a binary feature type, descriptiveness to inversions of spatial axes and contrast invariance to local images, utilizing a novel comparison method of smoothed images.  It combines vector features using the weighted sum of individual element comparisons, employing direction-dependent weights derived from optimal orientation estimation.  The introduction of contrast-invariant features addresses a critical shortcoming in 3D image feature sets, although it has been recognized that existing approaches can be overly descriptive due to invariant translations of spatial axes.  By combining contrast-invariance with spatial axis inversion, the proposed approach achieves a more descriptive and locally relevant set of image features.  The algorithm was tested using the Ben-Hashem dataset and published code will be made available at http://www.ias.inpot.it/research/3D-symmetry.html.

We've analyzed the data from a unique binary star system, SDSS J082239.54+304857.19, based on our comprehensive photometry observations taken over 618 days. These observations revealed detailed insights into the binary's behavior and allowed us to refine the time of eclipse, which shifted by about 8 minutes compared to previous records. Using this updated information, we've conducted a precise analysis of the binary's light curve and found that the stars' temperatures are likely very close to 6500 K. This finding, combined with our other results, has allowed us to make a more accurate estimate of the binary's distance, which is approximately 1670 pc. Furthermore, our research suggests that the cooler star, which is likely the primary star, has a mass of about 1.2 solar masses and is about 1.5 solar radii in size, while the hotter star, which is the secondary star, has a mass of around 1.1 solar masses and is about 1.8 solar radii in size. This estimate is consistent with the model's predictions for the long-term changes in the binary's orbital parameters. Additionally, our research indicates that the secondary star is likely to experience significant expansion due to mass transfer from the primary star in about 240 million years, at a rate of about 8 solar masses over the next 230 million years.

In numerous machine learning models and tasks, the implementation of global pooling operations is often based on experience rather than a thorough theoretical understanding. To address this, a novel, well-established global pooling framework has been developed through the lens of optimal transport theory. We demonstrate that most current global pooling methods are essentially specialized solutions to an unbalanced optimal transport problem. By allowing the parameters of this problem to be learned, various global pooling methods are unified within a single framework. Consequently, a generalized global pooling layer for neural networks called UOT-Pooling (UOTP) has been proposed. To implement this UOTP layer, the classic Sinkhorn-scaling algorithm is employed. Furthermore, a new model architecture based on the Bregman ADMM algorithm is designed, which offers better numerical stability and improved ability to reproduce existing pooling layers. Through experiments, the ability of the UOTP layer to accurately mimic nearly 20 different global pooling methods was verified, while also providing the advantage of end-to-end training. Furthermore, the code and data for these experiments can be accessed at https://github.com/jaymouss/uotp.

The primary objective of this research is to examine aspects of the validity of the active galactic nucleus unification theory. Our focus lies on a set of 34 AGNs, classified into two categories - those with type 1 nuclei and others with different types. We have also included 34 starburst galaxies in the comparison. Our analysis reveals that type 1 AGNs exhibit a link between the orientation of their nuclear structure and orientation of host galaxies. In contrast, the same correlation does not apply to other types of AGNs. Additionally, the host galaxies of radio-quasars show different characteristics than those of other types of AGNs, highlighting the necessity of further investigation into the unification theory's validity.

This paper delves into a comprehensive analysis of general rotational surfaces in the 4-dimensional Euclidean space, focusing on flat general rotation surfaces characterized by a 1-type Gauss map. Additionally, it's established that a non-planar, flat general rotation surface with this distinct Gauss map is a Lie group if and only if it's a Clifford torus.

Deep neural network training for semantic segmentation requires considerable effort,
so many researchers opt for pre-trained models to streamline the process.
Typically, these pre-trained models are developed using images from
classification tasks like object detection, but these may not align with the
required segmentation standards. A novel approach involves utilizing video data
to pre-train depth estimation models, which can then be modified to calculate
segmentation. This method leverages video information to improve the accuracy
of object boundaries within the scene, thereby enhancing segmentation outcomes.
Our research demonstrates that the DEPSI method, which combines video-based depth
estimation and domain adaptation to achieve semantic segmentation, outperforms
current state-of-the-art models on standard benchmarks. Moreover, the DEPSI
method's reliance on unlabeled video data eliminates the need for extensive
labor-intensive labeling processes.

The ability to create complex, engaging stories about the characteristics and behaviors of time-series data is extremely important in fields like geology, meteorology, epidemiology, finance, trade analysis, stock market monitoring, and sales forecasting. Currently, domain-specific time-series narration methods rely on predefined templates that ensure consistency but often produce mechanical, uninspired narratives. In contrast, we introduce TCube, a neural framework that can describe time-series data in a universal way without being tied to a particular domain. TCube represents essential time-series elements using a knowledge graph, which is then translated into coherent, engaging stories by leveraging the strengths of pre-trained language models. Since there's a scarcity of labeled data for time-series, TCube incorporates a knowledge graph to make the translation process feasible. This innovative approach marks TCube as the first exploration of neural methods for time-series narration, according to our current knowledge. In our comprehensive evaluations, we demonstrate that TCube significantly improves the variety of words in the generated stories, while also maintaining correct grammar, by up to 65.38%. Furthermore, an expert review of 21 professionals showed that 76.2% of them preferred TCube as a viable system for time-series narration because of its richer narratives, despite being auto-generated. TCube's open-source code and supporting materials are publicly available for anyone to reproduce our results and build upon our work.

The ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) has achieved precise measurements in two areas, namely neutral B meson mixing and CP violation, as well as in rare electroweak processes occurring in suppressed B-meson decays. This study concentrates on recent findings from the ATLAS collaboration, encompassing evaluations of rare occurrences like $B^0_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ and $B^0 \to \mu^+\mu^-$ decays and the determination of CP-violating processes in $B^0_s \to J/\psi\phi$.
On a Cayley tree, we analyze the Ising model and find novel periodic measures that are linked to index-2 normal subgroups within its group representation.

This study explores the well-posedness of global solutions, dependence on initial data, and potential loss of regularity in strictly hyperbolic equations with certain properties. We demonstrate that when coefficients exhibit (1,1) or (2,2) blow-up behavior, solutions to the Gevrey class and smooth class are drastically different. Furthermore, (1,1) or (2,2) smooth dependence does not imply the same in the Gevrey class, and (1,1) smooth dependence does not necessitate (2,2) smooth dependence, among other key findings.

This research introduces a novel application of the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network to tackle the challenging task of Japanese word segmentation. Building on previous breakthroughs in Chinese word segmentation using LSTM and GRU, this study tackles the more complex task of Japanese word segmentation which involves various character types such as hiragana, katakana, and kanji. These characters lead to significant orthographic variations and increase the difficulty of accurately segmenting Japanese words. To address this complexity, this study proposes an LSTM-based model for Japanese word segmentation, taking into consideration the essential global context. Experimental outcomes confirm that the proposed model attains exceptional accuracy when evaluated across different Japanese corpora.

On the Stack Overflow platform, users utilize 11,926,354 external connections to share relevant off-site information, augmenting the existing knowledge base. This collaborative effort involves repeated link sharing activities, where 82% of all links are external and 57% consist of frequently shared resources. To streamline users' knowledge management, this study delves into the characteristics of these shared links to identify common patterns in external resources and their cyclic usage. Our analysis reveals a significant increase in the number of links being shared, with the top domains accumulating a substantial 71.5% of all shared activities. Additionally, our research exposes vulnerabilities in user information and copyright infringement related to the shared links. This data offers insights into the dynamics of Stack Overflow's knowledge growth and highlights the importance of maintaining a stable structure in users' information sharing activities.

Galactic rotation curves show a range of varying inner slopes. Observations suggest a potential relationship between a galaxy's brightness and its central dark matter, indicating the need for a more comprehensive explanation. This study investigates various theoretical models that account for galaxy diversity, specifically comparing a Self-Interacting Dark Matter model with isothermal core to Cold Dark Matter models with/without baryonic feedback. Contrary to standard CDM, SIDM can form isothermal cores, and its effectiveness isn't largely influenced by long-term baryonic feedback processes. Utilizing the rotation curves of 90 galaxies from the SPARC catalog, a thorough model comparison is conducted to improve upon previous methodological issues. Our results show that the best-fitting halo models adhere to standard CDM concentration-mass relations. Although SIDM and feedback-influenced CDM outperform the non-feedback CDM in accounting for rotation curves of galaxies with varying surface brightnesses, neither model has a strong statistical advantage when compared to each other in explaining galaxy diversity in the given sample.

Although climate change is widely accepted, meaningful conversations about it are scarce,
resulting in slow implementation of the necessary societal changes to mitigate its effects.
To enhance climate communication and promote individual actions, we are developing a system
that leverages climate information and individual goals. 
First, we are creating a knowledge base that collects relevant climate data and second, we
are working on a recommendation system that provides tailored information to individuals based on their specific needs.
Our goal is to encourage climate conversations among family members and friends by sharing
personal experiences and sharing useful information to drive collective action. 
In this paper, we will outline the structure of our knowledge base and explain the reasoning behind our approach to climate communication.

Clinical symptoms recorded in unstructured doctor's notes are inaccessible for further use.
This problem can be resolved by using information extraction techniques capable of adapting to different medical settings and professionals. 
In this research, we address the issue of extracting symptoms by using pre-trained and fine-tuned models, trained on diverse patient data, medical institutions, and specialties. 
To reduce dependency on specific data, we develop an adaptive strategy for extracting symptoms by temporarily removing commonly mentioned symptoms from the original data source.
Also, our proposed approach pre-trains the language model using relevant but unmarked text for enhanced data representation. 
Experimental results show that incorporating these strategies significantly enhances symptom extraction accuracy when comparing source and target datasets.

Deep reinforcement learning stands out as a promising AI paradigm for creating autonomous systems, including automated driving. However, the application of supervised learning is generally preferred in developed environments due to its faster training times and higher performance. The key challenge in adopting supervised learning lies in gaining extensive annotated data for complex autonomous driving tasks. Cross-modal reinforcement learning offers a potential solution by leveraging available image data to create labeled information for training. In this research, we explore the cross-modal approach using video and pose annotations to train a system that tracks pedestrians. The project focuses on using video data to predict the future trajectory of a pedestrian based on their past movements. The model is evaluated on the Argoverse challenge dataset and compared with baseline performance. The study indicates that the cross-modal method achieves comparable results to the baseline approach while requiring significantly fewer annotations.

In recent years, AI networks, specifically those based on artificial neural systems, have significantly outperformed competitors in a wide range of tasks. However, the immense computational requirements for training and operational purposes have posed considerable challenges. Proponents of neuromorphic computing systems, which are inspired by the brain's fundamental processes, argue that this type of computation holds greater potential for efficiency and scalability. We present a novel framework for training neural networks that utilizes neurons that fire and fade, which builds on prior research and is supported by extensive empirical data. Our model can be trained end-to-end using a supervised or unsupervised approach and has been successfully applied to various challenging tasks, including the classification of images, recognition of speech, and solving complex mathematical problems. Notably, our model demonstrates comparable performance to existing top-notch models while achieving substantial speed and efficiency gains.

This research investigates the thermodynamic characteristics of spin-polarized strange quark matter under a specific magnetic field at finite temperature, applying the MIT bag model. Furthermore, we derived the equation of state for spin-polarized strange quark matter in the presence of a magnetic field, and subsequently, we examined the effects of these conditions on the structure of neutron stars. Our analysis reveals that the presence of spin-polarization and a finite temperature has a significant impact on the mass-radius relations of neutron stars. Our calculations indicate that for spin-polarized strange quark matter with no net baryon charge, an increase in temperature or magnetic field results in a smaller neutron star radius. Even at a temperature of 50 MeV, we found that the radius of a neutron star made of spin-polarized strange quark matter is significantly smaller than the radius formed at the same temperature from ordinary (spin-polarization free) strange quark matter. However, as the temperature decreases, the radius of a neutron star formed from spin-polarized strange quark matter at high magnetic fields (100 MeV) is closer to the radius formed at the same temperature from ordinary strange quark matter.

A surge in personal device ownership offers an immense, yet largely underutilized, potential source of computational power through volunteer computing. Leveraging the Pando platform can simplify the process of harnessing this potential by facilitating the distribution of parallel compute tasks, regardless of varying device capabilities and capacities. To evaluate Pando's effectiveness, we conducted a study that compared its performance in tackling different computational challenges. Our experiment design incorporated three distinct datasets and workloads one focused on data analysis, another on data simulation, and the third an optimization problem. Results from a 28-day test period indicated significant potential in volunteer-based computing, with notable evidence of convergence in solutions, despite some residual bias. Our investigation also aimed to explore the impact of evolving node collections on performance, a phenomenon we observed but did not anticipate.

A computational method for resolving nonlinear eigenvalue problems is presented, using an approximating function derived from the eigenvalues of a modified eigenproblem equation.  By utilizing a variable sampling process that focuses data collection on the areas most critical to solution resolution, this algorithm efficiently distributes resources. It then employs the collected information to produce approximations for the sought-after eigenvalues and eigenvectors through further processing. Several numerical demonstrations highlight the performance of this solution strategy.

We demonstrate the topological equivalence of all intermediate beta-transformations with a specific type of greedy beta-transformation that incorporates a hole at zero. By employing this equivalence, we obtain a detailed characterization of these transformations, yielding new insights and results in various areas, such as Krieger embeddings, survivor sets, Hausdorff dimensions, bifurcation sets, and badly approximable numbers. We show that certain classes of sets associated with these beta-transformations possess unique properties, specifically that they are winning in Schmidt games and have the countable intersection property.

We've found that gauge theories with $SO(N_{c})$ as a gauge group and matter fields represented as vectors confine, resulting from monopole condensation and the quark bilinear breaking $SU(N_{F})$ chiral symmetry down to $SO(N_{F})$. Our findings derive from an ${\cal N}=1$ supersymmetric theory, specifically with anomaly-mediated supersymmetry breaking.

Machine learning model interpretations are challenging, particularly when understanding how individual data points are classified. To address this, researchers have developed methods to provide insights into the critical regions of data points that contribute to their classification in tree ensemble models. However, these methods struggle with high-dimensional data and often generate many important regions that collectively fail to offer a clear understanding of each data point's critical aspects. To overcome this, researchers proposed Disentangled Attribution Curves (DEC), a novel method for each data point's interpretation by isolating key variables and their bounds. DEC effectively attributes variables to individual data points by selecting only the most relevant variables, thus providing clear and easy-to-interpret results for high-dimensional data. Furthermore, DEC's performance is comparable to state-of-the-art methods in evaluating its applicability across various datasets.

In federated learning, multiple parties collaborate on training machine learning models by sharing local parameters, rather than sensitive data. Despite this setup, model parameter exchanges can potentially expose confidential information, necessitating novel approaches for mitigation. Recent proposals, rooted in concepts such as multi-party computation and homomorphic encryption, often come at a cost of significant computational overhead, rendering them unsuitable for practical application. This work presents an alternative solution by harnessing the capabilities of Trusted Execution Environments to safeguard data and model interactions, specifically introducing Flatee - an efficient federated learning framework across these environments, that substantially minimizes both training and communication times, while remaining robust against adversarial manipulation.

The embedded systems industry is massive and ubiquitous, as evidenced by its presence in most of the world's produced processors. Interactions between drivers and external components like sensors and actuators pose significant challenges to embedded software development, particularly during the testing phase. Factors such as environmental unpredictability, limited hardware availability, and costs often hinder effective testing. To address these issues, this research presents a novel testing framework that targets driver verification on microcontrollers. The proposed solution involves a device under test, a duplicating counterpart, and a central control unit. The control unit manages testing procedures while the device under test runs the code being tested and its counterpart simulates the interactions with external peripherals. The effectiveness of the solution was validated through various test protocols.

This paper introduces a new method called Timeloops for automating system call filtering policies in containerized applications. During operation, Timeloops can automatically determine the system calls a program should be permitted to make and prevent unauthorized system calls from being made. In addition, Timeloops rectifies various shortcomings of static analysis-based techniques, such as the creation of highly precise filters and handling of programs that dynamically change execution paths. Our study showcases the capabilities of Timeloops by implementing system call filters for 12 widely used services and 5 distinct attacks, and demonstrates that it surpasses static analysis-based methods in precision by a significant margin. For example, while static analysis-based methods fail to filter out unapproved system calls in 23 instances, Timeloops succeeds in filtering them out in all 23 instances. Furthermore, our study validates the practicality of Timeloops by implementing a prototype in real-world environments, and reveals its capacity to prevent a range of malicious behavior.

Advanced techniques for representing complex data in compact, high-quality forms involve the embedding of product spaces.
We've identified a new challenge - linear classification in complex product space structures, which encompasses various geometric shapes such as flat, spherical, and hyperbolic environments.
To tackle this problem, we first establish a framework for defining linear classification models within curved, high-dimensional spaces characterized by 'k'-dimensional manifolds that can be generalized across multiple curvatures.
Next, we demonstrate the capability of one specific type of linear classification model to effectively represent complex data across diverse geometric spaces by comparing its performance with that of another model in a study involving synthetic data.
Furthermore, our analysis extends to real-world applications, such as learning latent features in fashion data, which confirms that the proposed model can also achieve similar results in practical scenarios.

This introduction focuses on stochastic Model Predictive Control methods that account for uncertainty in constraints, illustrated through a linear system under unpredictable conditions. The corresponding Matlab code is also accessible online for reference purposes.

This paper bridges the gap between compressed sensing and statistical learning, leveraging sparsity and structure to minimize the computational burden of learning tasks. We focus on independent component analysis through a compressive lens, demonstrating that certain properties within the cumulant-based ICA model yield a compact set of solutions that can be effectively represented within the cumulant tensor space. Utilizing a property that ensures randomness and coherence, we establish the existence of a compressive ICA scheme and propose two novel algorithms, IPG and ASD, to realize the compressed order through experimental verification. The CICA performance was evaluated using synthetic and real-world data sets, with experimental outcomes confirming its superiority to established methods. Furthermore, the concept of sparsity enables the application of CICA to scenarios where the number of data samples is less than the dimensionality of the given vector.

To analyze the interplay of species competition and dispersal, an asymmetrical noisy voter model was developed for a regular lattice structure. The model allows one species to colonize nearest-neighbor sites, while another species can settle at any distance but is less successful in doing so. The model includes external noise, which can lead to random species swaps in the lattice. The combination of these dynamics results in various species competition outcomes, including the exclusion of one species, distinct population coexistence, or bistable coexistence dependent on the starting population ratio. The model shows that an abrupt transition occurs when the dispersal distance threshold is crossed, and this transition can be predicted by calculating the model's largest Lyapunov exponent and exponent of nearest neighbor autocorrrelation.
We prove that von Neumann algebras associated with compact regions within abelian quantum double models have infinite type $II$.

To enhance magnon-photon-phonon entanglement in cavity magnomechanics, we develop an approach incorporating a coherent feedback loop. Furthermore, our findings confirm that both the steady and dynamic states of this system exhibit genuine tripartite entanglement. We utilize the logarithmic negativity to quantify quantum correlations between individual subsystems, as well as genuine tripartite entanglement through a nonzero minimum residual contangle. We investigate experimentally feasible parameters that enable the generation of tripartite entanglement and demonstrate its significant enhancement with coherent feedback by adjusting the beam splitter's reflective parameter. Additionally, the effects of photon loss in the cavity and phonon loss in the oscillator on quantum correlations are explored, revealing that the system remains entangled even in the presence of moderate dissipation. This finding has potential applications in experiments seeking to preserve entanglement over longer periods.

We've obtained one-loop triple-collinear splitting operators for color and spin spaces, applicable to all five scenarios: $q \to qq'\bar{q}'$, $q \to qq\bar{q}$, $q \to qgg$, $g \to gq\bar{q}$ and $g \to ggg$. The exact expressions are derived within dimensionless QCD and include the results of a specific integral up to its second-order expansion. Additionally, we've evaluated the associated splitting functions. Our results are crucial and necessary for creating subtraction and integrated-subtraction terms in next-to-next-to-next-to leading order cross-section computations.

A formal proof for the Neron Desingularization, a multidimensional case algorithm, has been formulated and applied to one-dimensional local rings, and this concept is currently being used within Singular software implementation. Furthermore, a relevant theorem based on Greenberg's Strong Approximation theorem has also been introduced and applied to the realm of one-dimensional local rings.

Ancient sundials served as primary timekeepers before the invention of mechanical clocks, with the classical Islamic civilization utilizing the Sun's daily movement to determine prayer times, often relying on sundials for this purpose. This knowledge eventually spread to Indonesia through Islamic cultural influences. Indonesian sundials developed as a reflection of local advancements in astronomy, technology, art, and architecture, with historical examples warranting detailed documentation and study, though often overlooked in existing literature. To collect necessary spatial and temporal information on these sundials, a citizen science initiative could be implemented, addressing research inquiries while promoting science education among the general public. This concept has been proposed as a framework, referred to as the Suryakala-Nusantara program, to explore sundials through citizen science methods.

This research focuses on an integrated data and energy transmission network, which incorporates D2D communication. This hybrid network allows a central hub to transfer data to those in need and supply power to those who require it. This coexistence also allows D2D transmissions to use the same bandwidth. This integrated network is critical in addressing future energy and spectrum shortages. However, these D2D transmissions and wireless link losses could significantly impede the data transfer rate. In response to this challenge, we propose introducing an intelligent reflecting surface. We then develop an optimization problem to maximize the data transfer rate while ensuring that power is generated and D2D communication speeds are met. This optimization problem requires significant computational resources, but we develop an algorithm that addresses this challenge with reduced computational demands. Finally, simulations confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

The surge in telework needs has highlighted the potential benefits of fully
automating and controlling experiments remotely. This work presents the technical
advancements of creating a two-dimensional LDV measurement system using a single-
point LDV system via a remotely controllable and automated setup. The document's
aim is to expedite the development of similar setups for this kind of application,
which is highly versatile and can be applied to various scenarios including both
air-based acoustic signal-driven samples and mechanically induced samples.

The cardinalities of finite models for sentences with at least three variables and binary relations are examined in this study.  Specifically, we demonstrate that any such sentence has a finite set of possible model cardinalities which can be calculated deterministically.  Furthermore, we establish that the spectrum of any such sentence contains the maximum possible number of model cardinalities relative to its type, with at least half of the possible model cardinalities belonging to the same type.  It's also shown that the spectrum of any such sentence is extensive, with an infinite number of model cardinalities and a wide range of isomorphism types.  Finally, we determine the maximum possible number of model cardinalities for de Morgan lattices and distributive lattices with at least three variables and binary relations.

The effectiveness of programmable electrostatic phase plates is subject to debate 
given their varying suitability for particular applications. Our study delves into 
alternative designs of phase plates specifically tailored to mitigate spherical 
aberration in Transmission Electron Microscopes (TEMs). Through numerical analysis, 
we investigate the potential for a phase plate to attain down to 1 Angstrom 
resolution on an uncorrected TEM. By examining various design features 
(fill-factor, pixel pattern, symmetry), we identify how they influence the electron 
probe size and current density. Our proposed designs exhibit probe sizes ($d_{50}$) 
as low as 0.66 Angstrom, indicating that a programmable phase plate with 
electrostatic elements can successfully rectify spherical aberration well beyond the 
1 Angstrom threshold.

Drawing inspiration from Feynman's and Deutsch's groundbreaking work, we introduce a theoretical framework that assesses computational capability across diverse physical platforms and complexity scales. This framework is utilized to analyze the fundamental principles of quantum computation. Furthermore, this study serves as a precursor to investigating more universal computation models by examining additional physical mechanisms exemplified throughout the paper.

This study focused on determining the general equation for calculating the potential positions of an $n$ step random walk in a $d$ dimensional space with a single unit step size, denoted as $|P_n^{d}|$. Our approach began by establishing a recursive relationship for the count formula: $|P_n^{d+1}| = |P_n^d| + 2\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} |P_k^d|$. We then presented two distinct methods to derive an explicit equation for $|P_n^{d}|$, involving the application of generating functions and Faulhaber's formula. Ultimately, our findings were presented in a matrix representation as our primary theorem.

This research in depth investigates the model of spherically symmetric polymer black holes, which was first introduced by Gambini, Olmedo, and Pullin within the framework of loop quantum gravity. We explored how in the GOP model the spacelike transition surface at the classical singularity replaces it. Utilizing transformations in the coordinates, the authors were able to extend the metric to the white hole region, which led to discovering that the structure of the quantum black hole bears resemblance to that of wormholes, with their radii equal to each other. Moreover, the authors found that not only is the throat, but also the horizons and the spatial infinities where the energy conditions are violated. This leads to the conclusion that the quantum effects are not confined solely to the spacetime geometry, but rather, they are extensive, influencing the quasinormal modes of black hole perturbations by altering their frequencies and damping rates. Furthermore, the authors found that the real part of the mode frequencies is positive, which confirms that the mode is damped rather than amplified.

We have derived a semi-analytical formula for the dynamic density-density correlation of massless Dirac electrons in doped graphene, which is applicable at finite temperatures. This finding is key to understanding the thermal screening of interactions among Dirac electrons and we leverage it to calculate the thermal capacity and compressibility of doped graphene. Notably, at very low temperatures, the thermal capacity displays a linear temperature dependence characteristic of normal Fermi liquids, with the coefficient controlled by the velocity of charge carriers in the material.

Continuous speech leads to consistent prosody patterns, yet current speech synthesis models often disregard context. These systems fall short when it comes to producing high-quality paragraphs, necessitating a system that integrates contextual elements. MaskedSpeech is a context-aware synthesis system addressing this limitation. By building upon a masking strategy, MaskedSpeech incorporates contextual acoustic features into each sentence, enabling a more detailed understanding of semantic relationships. Additionally, cross-sentence coarse-grained semantic features aid in the development of a natural prosody. Through augmenting masked acoustic features with contextual elements during training, MaskedSpeech outperformed baseline systems in expressiveness and naturalness.

We've enhanced projection predictive inference by streamlining its computational process and broadening its applicability to a variety of models and data types. The original algorithm, introduced by Solnon et al. in 2019, successfully combined the predictive information gained from projecting observations onto subspaces with respect to model parameters and the support of relevant variables, enabling efficient variable selection even in high-dimensional settings. However, this approach had limitations: its slowness and lack of generalizability due to its reliance on specific summation formulas over subspaces. Our improvements address these shortcomings: we've accelerated projection predictive inference and expanded its scope to a broader class of models and data types. The resulting algorithm is now more user-friendly, providing feasible variable selection options and efficient parameter estimation for various models, including sparsity-based models, state-based models, and multi-layer models, in a range of settings, such as univariate and functional data, and network-based models.

Recent research has demonstrated that Deep Neural Networks are susceptible to strategically crafted malicious inputs, prompting the development of countermeasures against query-optimization attacks. Our research diverges from previous studies by exploring the vulnerability of DNN models to Man-in-the-Middle attacks. From an attacker's standpoint, conventional adversarial attacks prove ineffective as they necessitate multiple interactions with the model prior to execution, whereas MitM attacks can launch without this limitation. Moreover, these attacks can only be applied to existing data sets, significantly diminishing the attacker's yield. Conversely, employing generative models can mitigate these drawbacks, enabling the creation of novel adversarial examples. Specifically, our analysis delves into the capability of generative models, particularly Variational Auto-Encoders, in creating adversarial examples. Our proposed approach utilizes a VAE decoder to generate malicious inputs or transform benign outputs into adversarial examples. Our results show that our method enables successful MitM attacks on both MNIST and CIFAR10 datasets at an impressive rate, rivaling the effectiveness of existing query-optimization attacks. Moreover, our approach boasts considerable efficiency, executing 104 times faster than state-of-the-art query-optimization attacks.

Climate change communication is complicated by the proliferation of conspiracy theories, particularly those found online. This research investigates prevalent conspiracy theories regarding climate change by analyzing a significant Twitter dataset and applies a sophisticated stance detection technique. Our analysis focuses on whether such conspiracy theories are more widely shared by those who do not believe in climate change or those who do. Furthermore, we examine the most popular conspiracy theories, their variations with differing levels of climate change acceptance, and reveal that non-believers predominantly disseminate messages containing conspiracy theory-related keywords. Notably, all conspiracy theories are not equally prevalent. Our findings also highlight their implications for effective climate change communication strategies.

A study focused on the production of dark matter in proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV has been carried out using the CMS detector. This study analyzed a dataset of 35.9 fb^-1 of collisions. It differs from earlier studies which focused solely on dark matter creation accompanied by a top quark pair by also investigating cases where a top quark was present individually. Multiple criteria for selecting data categories that correspond to either a top quark or a top quark pair were developed to determine the outcomes of this study. No notable discrepancies with respect to the standard model predictions were discovered during the analysis. It was established that certain creation scenarios for dark matter in the form of scalar or pseudoscalar mediator particles are inconsistent with experimental data at a 95% confidence level if their masses do not exceed 60 GeV or 100 GeV respectively. It was also established that the range of cross-sections for the direct scattering of dark matter with top quarks which are consistent with experimental data range from 0.6 to 18 fb. It was further established that the range of cross-sections for the indirect production of dark matter in association with top quarks which are consistent with experimental data range from 0.4 to 50 fb.

Given an n-exangulated category with specified properties, we establish that it satisfies Auslander-Reiten-Serre duality if and only if it possesses certain duality-based angles. We also determine a specific condition necessary for the presence of Serre duality. Assuming duality exists, we establish a one-to-one correspondence involving a bijection and specific category characteristics.

Building upon Kirkeboen et al.'s (2016) work that demonstrates the feasibility of combining multiple treatment instruments with ranked preference data, we analyze the testable implications of the key assumptions underpinning their identification argument. This analysis also offers a novel assessment of the biases resulting from these assumption violations. Ultimately, these findings empower researchers to evaluate the reliability of these assumptions and determine the practical impact of their breaches. Utilizing the identified method, we investigate the post-secondary field of study return on investment in Norway and Denmark, exploring potential cross-country differences. Our results indicate significant correlation between fields of study return on investment in both countries, particularly after eliminating fields where identification assumption breaches occur.

To advance our understanding of matter's various forms, high-energy particle collisions with a wide variety of projectiles must be studied extensively.
Although scientists have utilized beams of numerous particles to make significant breakthroughs, creating and working with beams of antineutrons, specific hyperons and their counterparts has been notoriously challenging.
However, a recent high-tech research setup known as a super $J/\psi$ factory holds the potential to greatly improve access to these elusive particles. As a result, a huge number of $J/\psi$ decays occur annually, creating favorable conditions to accurately analyze these interactions using precision-tagging of co-produced particles. 
This state-of-the-art technology can facilitate groundbreaking studies of diverse targets and open doors for new particle and nuclear physics applications, such as studying antinucleon-nucleon interaction, properties of strange nucleons and nucleon-like particles, (anti)hyperon-nucleon interaction, exotic light hadrons and more, along with advancing our understanding of hypernuclei, calibration of computational simulations in hadronic physics and medicine, and exploring numerous other related topics.

Most of a multiple star system's final mass is accumulated during the first few million years of its existence, specifically during the protostellar and protoplanetary phases.  Past research on binary systems has shown that in these systems, the majority of the acquired mass is typically added to the less massive star, resulting in mass equalization.  Yet, young stellar groups are frequently composed of more than two stars that are predicted to exist in a hierarchical setup.  Notwithstanding the significant astrophysical relevance of this issue, little research has been devoted to understanding differential mass acquisition in systems consisting of three or more stars.  We carried out a study aimed at determining whether the trends of mass acquisition predicted for binary systems are applicable to more complex systems consisting of three or more stars.  Utilizing three-dimensional Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics simulations, our research team used the code Phantom to simulate the growth of both binary systems and hierarchical triples within a surrounding disc of gas and dust.  We identified distinct patterns of mass acquisition in systems consisting of three stars and found notable differences between these patterns and those seen in binary systems.  These distinctions are attributed to interactions between the less massive binary in these systems and surrounding disc material.  Notably, our research revealed that in systems consisting of three stars, the less massive binary in these systems accumulates more mass than would be expected in binary systems if the less massive binary in these systems were solitary. This manuscript examines flat spacetimes with intrinsic properties, as viable models for understanding the universe on a cosmological scale. We find that such spacetimes naturally incorporate geometric patterns suitable for describing irregular, periodically-distributed matter within the universe. We also establish mathematical proofs for their local representation, as well as the existence and uniqueness of the Einstein's equations under these specific spatial constraints. Notably, our research uncovers an interesting set of precise solutions, illustrating how these spacetimes can be used in cosmology to model a universe transitioning from homogenous, isotropic states in the early stages to more complex distributions with voids and matter peaks over time.

This paper presents a novel, multi-stage image segmentation model, combining the techniques of image restoration and image segmentation. The integration of image restoration aspects enables the proposed model to effectively handle images corrupted by noise, blurriness, missing pixels, and varied color schemes. Specifically, this approach extends the influential Mumford-Shah model, allowing for improved segmentation of gray-scale and vector-valued images affected by noise, blurriness, or missing data. Our model can be efficiently optimized using the alternating minimization algorithm, which converges under minimal conditions. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior segmentation results, particularly for blurry images and those with missing pixel values, outperforming existing state-of-the-art segmentation models.

Active galactic nuclei (AGNs), a class of active supermassive black holes, allow us to study the mass and spin of their central black holes through the analysis of their electromagnetic spectra. By using the disk radiation model, we can determine the mass and spin of the black holes, but the accuracy of these determinations depends on the accuracy of the model. Notably, a similar approach has been developed to study the basis of standard thin-disk models, which assumes all energy is emitted from the surface of the disk. However, high-energy radiation originates not only from the surface but also from the hot inner areas near the black hole. We have developed a new approach for modeling disk radiation that takes into account break in temperature near the central black hole's event horizon without specifying the physical cause of this break. By using this model, we can determine the basis of spectra that take into account the black hole's spin without being confined to the simple model of standard thin-disk models. We have applied our new approach to the highest-energy AGN, known as Mrk 110, using the largest space telescope, at a wavelength of 2200 angstroms. As a result, we have obtained more accurate estimates of its black hole's mass and spin, which is approximately 0.9 aromatic for a non-rotating black hole. We have further demonstrated that our new approach can be used in the study of other AGNs by analyzing the basis of their spectra.

We introduce LoiCalEmu, a free and open-source simulator for the Loicalo AI chip, which is a novel computing solution that combines the benefits of neuromorphic and conventional computing methods. The Loicalo AI chip is designed to handle complex data processing tasks by integrating spiking neural networks and general-purpose computing through a innovative bus system. However, implementing the full system on a hardware platform poses significant challenges due to the intricate interconnection of hardware components and the scarcity of programming tools. To overcome these limitations, we've developed an advanced emulator named LoiCalEmu, which accurately replicates the behavior of the Loicalo AI chip across its hardware components. The emulator features a multi-threaded design that streamlines task execution for both CPU-based programming tasks and neural network simulations. Moreover, the emulator includes a plug-in architecture that enables users to create custom extensions for their specific use cases. With these innovative features, the LoiCalEmu emulator has the potential to facilitate the rapid development of applications for the Loicalo AI chip.

A solar type-I noise storm is created by particle beams accelerated from active regions experiencing significant changes. These storms exhibit significant intensity fluctuations in very short time frames and on very short wavelengths. This study explores the dynamic evolution of a solar type-I noise storm associated with a microflare. Observations conducted at OI 630.9 nm reveal two distinct modes of evolution - rapid intensification and gradual growth. The rapid intensification phase is influenced by competing processes including the increase in particle flux and growth of the storm source, while the gradual growth phase is driven by the expansion of the storm base and strengthening of the electron acceleration. The storm intensity is ultimately determined by the balance of these factors and the mean electron density within the storm.

A compact magneto-optical trap has been successfully developed, using a planar-integrated design that merges an optical grating chip and a magnetic coil chip. This novel setup minimizes the size and weight of the trap, requiring only a single laser beam to capture a population of approximately 10,000 cold rubidium atoms. The improved MOT architecture has potential applications in devices such as gravimeters, atomic clocks, and optical springs, offering a reduction in volume, weight, and complexity.

The process of supermassive black hole growth, known as accretion, is heavily influenced by the properties of the surrounding gas cloud, including its angular momentum. Researchers have long speculated that conservation of angular momentum could limit the rate at which gas clouds feed black holes.
