This work proposes a solution to this problem by employing a family of quantum estimators known as the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE), which does not rely on highly entangled states and instead uses less entangling measurements. By demonstrating the consistent estimation error in scenarios where multiple measurements are taken, this research shows that MLE can provide more accurate estimates than previously thought, specifically in parameter estimation using Henderson Mitchell and Kluzniak Kazimiercz states. Furthermore, this research expands on existing research in this area by incorporating probing strategies that use less entangling measurements, thereby enhancing the precision of quantum estimators while decreasing the required measurements.

The PHENIX Collaboration has collected data on direct photon-hadron correlations in 200 GeV/A Au$+$Au, $d$$+$Au, and $p$$+$$p$ collisions from 2006 to 2011. These findings reveal that cold nuclear matter does not significantly influence $d$$+$Au collisions. A notable disparity exists between hadrons carrying a large fraction of the quark's momentum and those that do not, as well as between Au$+$Au and $p$$+$$p$ collisions. This anomaly is more pronounced for hadrons resulting from higher momentum quarks. Calculations using a parton model in vacuum and nuclear matter explain the data reasonably well for both momentum ranges.

In this hybrid digital-analog approach to quantum computing, any quantum algorithm can be implemented without traditional two-qubit gates by utilizing an inherent, always-active connection between qubits. Building on this principle, our research explores how digital-analog simulation can be used to study fermionic systems, specifically the Fermi-Hubbard model, using a fermionic SWAP network and a method to correct distortions. Focusing on the effects of qubit connectivity and the distribution of interaction coefficients, as well as the precision of entanglement-inducing operations, our results indicate that an optimal qubit connectivity arrangement for simulating fermionic systems of any dimensionality is a chain for systems without spin and a ladder for those with spin. This relatively straightforward connectivity arrangement makes the digital-analog method particularly appealing for fermionic quantum simulations.

A common issue in machine learning lies in striking a balance between optimizing performance and robustly handling out-of-distribution (OoD) scenarios. Certain methods rely on complex penalty terms that adjust model behavior, but these tend to be underutilized due to 'over-shooting' and hence, fail to fully leverage the data. We propose 'Pre-Rich' - an innovative technique that initiates networks with a rich set of representations. Primed with this strong foundation, the model is better equipped to optimize its performance and also, more effectively handle OoD scenarios. Our experiments across various benchmarks confirm that Pre-Rich significantly enhances a range of methods and also, outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches.

Achieving the formation of intricate structures and rapid concentration of light within or through disordered mediums is an arduous endeavor due to variations in refractive index, unpredictable light scattering, and speckle noise generation. To address these challenges, we've developed a novel weighted-mutation-assisted genetic algorithm (WMA-GA) with an R-squared-based fitness function that enhances image clarity, precision, and rapid convergence in forming complex structures within scattering media. As a companion technology to our binary WMA-GA system, we've designed a swift, economical, and reliable iterative wavefront manipulation system that utilizes an affordable ferroelectric liquid crystal (FLC)-based binary-phase spatial light modulator (SLM). This wavefront manipulation system enables the creation of numerous complex 3D heterostructures with an unprecedented level of accuracy and at a relatively high speed of 12 frames per second. To validate our approach, we've successfully produced and visually confirmed several intricate structures, including a flower, the human profile, and the rotation of light cone formation in a scattering medium, all achieved with high spatial resolution and accuracy. Furthermore, we've explored and obtained experimental results for the formation of rotational symmetric structures such as the rotation of light cone and the formation of the Buddha head in a scattering medium using our proposed algorithm-assisted adaptive optics system.

We appreciate the discussion opportunity facilitated by editors and valuable input from discussants. Our work is influenced by the inspiring research of Kallus (2020), which enhances policy learning efficiency via retargeting. Building upon Dukes and Vansteelandt (2020), we distinguish our research from Kallus (2020) in Section 1 by highlighting their distinct assumptions, variations, and research objectives. In Section 2, guided by Li et al. (2020) and Liang and Zhao (2020), we analyze the efficient policy evaluation problem using data from both the training and testing distributions. Our results demonstrate that under specific growth conditions, efficient value function estimates can yield strong performance, although the rate may not surpass that of independent samples. In contrast, testing data is essential for achieving the optimal statistical rate in the context of policy evaluation. In Section 3, we emphasize the broad applicability of our research to general function estimation and highlight potential extensions to more intricate statistical estimation problems.

Monolithic CMOS sensors featuring small collection electrodes are advantageous due to high signal quality and low power consumption. However, these sensors have limited functionality due to the use of thin high-resistivity epitaxial layers during fabrication. In this study, researchers investigate the active sensor depth using the CLICTD technology, a small collection-electrode monolithic demonstrator. Particle beams are utilized to analyze the charge collection properties and device performance across different thicknesses under various beam angles. In CMOS sensors utilizing a high-resistivity Czochralski substrate, a notable enhancement is observed, with the sensitive volume increasing two-fold, subsequently yielding significant gains in detection efficiency and spatial/temporal resolution.

Advanced telescopes strive to spot planets at closer distances, lower masses, or older ages than ever before, with the ultimate goal of directly identifying habitable-zone planets with masses similar to those of Earth. Despite recent technological improvements, a significant barrier remains, with the ability of current high-tech ground-based telescopes limited by image speckles that obstruct our view. This challenge has made it difficult to effectively eliminate the distortions introduced by the atmosphere and the telescope's instruments themselves. To overcome this issue, researchers have proposed a new system known as the Fast Atmospheric Self-coherent camera (FAST), a wavefront sensing and control algorithm that enables the system to operate at the speed of milliseconds even when it detects extremely faint signals. We have successfully tested FAST in the laboratory, showcasing its capability to effectively eliminate the distortions introduced by the atmosphere at the speed of milliseconds.

This study presents a novel exogenous model to tackle the challenge of negative interest rates, maintaining the mathematical ease of the Cox-Ingersoll-Ross model, and accurately replicating the observed yield curve. It combines the difference between two separate Cox-Ingersoll-Ross processes, with one adjusted for the current short-term rate. To determine the relevant parameters, we utilize realistic initial conditions, and the result is a model that fits the average swaption volatility, as well as the one-year forward rate, observed between 2016 and 2020. Notably, this model yields positive, though slightly lowered, interest rates on average.

Research into the properties of neutrinos, specifically their behavior and production, is ongoing with various experiments such as LENS, its research findings are discussed within the context of current studies and future prospects for the investigation of sterile neutrinos and the development of a neutrino spin detector.

Meta-analyses that include multiple trials with related groups often employ cluster-robust variance estimators to account for within-cluster correlations. However, these estimators can become overly conservative when there are only a few study groups within each cluster, which is common in this type of analysis. Furthermore, conventional methods for testing heterogeneity and conducting confidence intervals may break down as a result. We have developed a testing method for heterogeneity that does not rely on normal assumptions and can handle small within-cluster sample sizes, along with a method for constructing robust confidence intervals. We compared the performance of this new approach with traditional methods through both theoretical assessments and a meta-analytic simulation based on real-data studies. Our results show that the new test outperforms conventional tests in terms of type I error rates and provides more accurate confidence intervals. We have also introduced a testing method for assessing whether within-cluster study outcomes are independent and normally distributed, which may be useful in identifying outliers and detecting anomalies within these study outcomes.

This study introduces an advanced integration method for simulating multiple steps of particle collisions in flows. Due to the need for smaller time steps for resolving particle collisions, traditional models can become computationally expensive for large-scale simulations involving numerous particles. Existing methods often involve artificially lengthening collision time steps to several times the time steps used in flow simulations, however this can lead to biased simulation results. Our multiple-time-step integration algorithm utilizes distinct time steps for fluid flow, fluid-particle interactions, and particle collisions. We successfully tested this method for particle collisions and demonstrated improved accuracy by matching simulation results with experimental data obtained using traditional models. Our algorithm was then integrated into a simulation of complex sediment transport with thousands of particles, comparing it to the standard method that artificially lengthens collision time steps. The results showed that artificially stretching collision time steps leads to particles being too flexible and affects the turbulence and distribution of particles, whereas our algorithm reduces computational cost to one tenth of the standard method while retaining nearly identical accuracy.

Investigating the source of radiation energy in the Unruh/Hawking process has shed new light on the particle number definition, particularly as it relates to conservation laws. Research has found that particle radiation is not a product of gravitational force-driven pair creation, but rather an outcome stemming from disparities in the laws governing particle number definition. In the far future, the source of emitted energy corresponds to zero-point fluctuations characterized by exponentially large wave numbers, prompting a reassessment of the black hole evaporation paradigm.

The effect of transverse momentum broadening on gluons within a hot medium is investigated using a bottom-up approach, starting from a factorization representation that ignores correlations between transverse momentum components. This analysis considers broadening to low-order approximation, focusing on gluon spectrum shapes and coefficients. Results from next-to-leading order perturbative QCD calculations are compared with leading order predictions from the color evolution framework. Gluon broadening spectrum shapes are sensitive to the medium response properties, with fast gluons influenced more than slow ones. A comparison with previous gluon broadening work is also conducted.

This article presents $2$ distinct proof methodologies establishing the existence of pairs of relatively prime positive integers, $a$ and $b$, for which the following congruence is satisfied: the expression $a^2+ab+b^2$ can be factored as $7$ raised to a power of $n$.

The video explores the dynamics of a liquid jet that enters a channel filled with the same fluid. As the jet interacts with the surrounding stream, it becomes encircled by a sheath of entrained air. This sheath plays a significant role in the dynamic behavior of the jet and its penetration into the stream. Additionally, we examine the instability effects that develop on the liquid jet and the consequences of these effects on its behavior in the context of fluid dynamics.

High-performance computing systems rely heavily on fault tolerance to prevent data loss and ensure system reliability. Recent advances in non-volatile memory have made it feasible to achieve this, as data in such memory is preserved even during crashes. Nevertheless, the volatility of system caches still poses a challenge, as data in these caches may be lost in the event of a crash, necessitating an explicit flush into the main memory to guarantee data integrity. In this study, a new algorithm-based approach is proposed to guarantee data consistency and correctness for high-performance computing applications in systems using non-volatile memory. This method introduces only a minor overhead, allowing developers to leverage the properties of algorithms to verify data integrity after system crashes. Our proposed approach demonstrates significant advantages over traditional checkpointing methods in terms of overhead, particularly for applications with long runtime periods. Our experiments further examine the implications of memory architecture on algorithm-based checkpointing and provide insights into the potential of this method to guarantee fault tolerance in high-performance computing systems.

Organizational frameworks like information hierarchies are commonly used to present complex data and simplify navigation, yet the automatic generation methods available today don't account for the interconnections in modern information networks. Presently, most techniques represent topics as abstract probabilities rather than tangible components of the underlying network, and many lack the scalability needed for web-based applications. In contrast, we propose a novel approach, Hierarchical Document Topic Model (HDTM), utilizing a non-parametric distributed processing model that effectively extracts meaningful hierarchies from large networks, even at a massive data scale, as evidenced by our experiments using three smaller datasets and Wikipedia's full content.

We conducted an exhaustive examination comparing the statistical properties of non-hierarchical three-body systems with corresponding theoretical models. By running and analyzing one million simulations for diverse initial conditions, both with and without equal masses in three-body systems, we were able to achieve precise statistical accuracy. Four distinct measures were used to characterize the distribution of ergodic disintegrations: the probability of escape for individual bodies, the exponent representing narrow escapes, the predicted absorption as a function of binary energy and angular momentum, and the distribution of lifetimes. Our results showed that escape probabilities align with theoretical predictions, highlighting how mass and energy affect predictions. Furthermore, the exponent representing narrow escapes and the predicted absorption as a function of binary energy and angular momentum matched theoretical models. Our analysis also revealed a power-law distribution of lifetimes with a slope that varies based on mass ratios. By correlating this with the predicted phase space structure, we provided a theoretical explanation for this power-law distribution.

The suppression of heavy vector mesons in high-energy nuclear collisions can occur due to several reasons, including quark-gluon condensation, parton energy loss, and the interaction of the meson with a deformed electromagnetic field. To investigate these effects, a theoretical framework is established, allowing for a comparative analysis of J/$\psi$ and $\psi$(2S) meson suppression. It is observed that only a specific type of deformed electromagnetic field can explain the difference in suppression between prompt and prompt-like non-prompt mesons, and this effect increases with atomic number. Additionally, the impact of deformed electromagnetic fields on $B$ mesons is considered.

We propose an arrangement of predicates in continuous logic such that the
logical framework's meaning can be structured within a hyperdoctrine framework.
This hyperdoctrine can be incorporated into a hyperdoctrine representing subobjects within a suitable category of topological structures. 
To achieve this incorporation, we first simplify the hyperdoctrine framework for continuous logic and establish an equivalence between its category of equivalence relations and that of complete metric spaces under uniform mappings.

When designing a software system, a modification in one component may
unintentionally impact other parts, hindering overall system performance. This is
addressed by conducting regression testing, which re-evaluates system sections
aimed at verifying their functionality. However, pinpointing these affected
areas remains challenging, making it essential to identify system changes through
advanced analysis methods. We propose an approach that uses data from system
performance and tests to pinpoint areas impacted by modifications, allowing
for more efficient and effective regression testing. By integrating these
sources of information, we create a mathematical model which can be solved to
locate the affected system sections when abnormalities are detected during
testing. We demonstrate the accuracy of this method through experiments on
real-world systems, also discussing possible extensions to improve its
accuracy and applicability.

A new technique is proposed to forecast suicidal ideation based on the integration of Electronic Health Records and Ecological Momentary Assessment data utilizing advanced deep sequential models. These datasets consist of asynchronous, variable-length, randomly sampled sequences which are modelled separately using Recurrent Neural Networks and combined through the alignment of hidden states, along with attention and pre-training schemes to handle differing sequence lengths. Experimental outcomes using 1023 patients' data demonstrate that the incorporation of Ecological Momentary Assessment records significantly increases the recall and precision of the forecast, outperforming conventional methods. Furthermore, the proposed method achieves enhanced generalizability across diverse patient populations when compared to traditional approaches.

Our research reports a significant $\sim 5\sigma$ discovery of polarized X-ray emission within a range of 3-6 keV originating from Cassiopeia A with the IXPE. Our findings reveal a combined polarization level of $2.8\pm0.3$%, obtained after summing the polarization vectors from a $20'$ radius circular area at a $4.5\sigma$ confidence level, or $1.7\pm0.3$% for a $10'$ radius circular area at a $3.5\sigma$ confidence level. Our data show that the emission up to $\sim 5$ keV holds a considerable portion of its total energy, nearly $40\pm10$% in intensity, in comparison to the iron emission at $\sim 6.4$ keV. We propose a comprehensive model to explain the observed emission, suggesting that the synchrotron radiation type X-rays are emitted by high-energy electrons moving in a magnetic field aligned with the remnant's center, or more specifically, within a $20^\circ$ of radius, based on our IXPE data, or possibly of the diffuse component, within a $1^\circ$ of radius, if the polarization level is $1.5$%. Our results imply a similar emission mechanism for the synchrotron radiation at the remnant's eastern edge, or more specifically, within a $1^\circ$ of radius, or more broadly

Consider a set $\{a_1, \ldots, a_n\}$ of distinct positive integers where $a_1 < \ldots < a_n$, with the requirement that only subset sums up to a size of at most $\lambda n$ be unique. Erdos originally proposed a conjecture suggesting that $a_n > c \cdot 2^n$, with the current record at $a_n > c \cdot 2^n/\sqrt{n}$. This article presents modified constraints where we investigate lower and upper bounds for the minimum possible value of $a_n$.

The characteristics of dense matter within the density range of 1-10 times nuclear saturation density, present in compact stars, are intriguingly ambiguous and may influence neutron star dynamics as observed from gravitational waves.  As a compact star's density increases, sound velocity approaches the conformal limit at high densities, satisfying the causality limit while its detailed behavior remains disputed. It's hypothesized that dense matter sound velocity can be an indicator of a deconfinement phase transition, possibly exhibiting a distinctive relationship with density. Our work delves into the fundamental properties of dense matter sound velocity and the adiabatic index within neutron stars, quark stars, and hybrid stars.  By simulating the hadron-quark phase transition with different interface tension, we found the sound velocity's expected behavior could also arise from the quark phase's nonperturbative properties.  Consequently, this could result in a denser star with similar mass, thus providing significant implications for measuring tidal deformabilities through gravitational wave observations.  Our study highlights the necessity for considering various dense matter phases and surface layer effects when constructing compact stars.  These findings can be tested by future gravitational wave detectors, enabling a deeper comprehension of dense matter and compact stars, thereby expanding our understanding of general relativity and stellar physics.

We investigate a variety of non-classical states made up of superposed, displaced number states and their effectiveness in optimizing sensitivity when measuring specific parameters. Our findings reveal that certain combinations of squeezing and displacement can significantly enhance the precision of parameter estimates, often outperforming highly squeezed state solutions. The optimal performance, however, consistently demands a specific form of displacement that varies depending on the parameter in question, indicating a general trend. The optimal displacement grows stronger for parameters that require larger amounts of squeezing and can be identified through a condition related to the state's superposition amplitude. The maximum possible sensitivity improvements can be achieved with minimal displacement, using purely Gaussian states, by choosing a displacement value equal to the square root of the number of photons in the state.

During gas-liquid interfaces that are subject to irregular movement such as splashing and atomization, the resulting fluid structures can be intricate and embedded in their surroundings. In this work, we employ a technique called skeletonization to extract the fundamental information needed to represent their geometry. By applying a modified version of a previous approach that efficiently captures the dynamics of multi-component flows with distinct interfaces, we successfully simplify the representation of a periodic liquid jet. This involves propagating a gradient through the structure and simultaneously adjusting its interfaces, ultimately leading to their convergence into the essential framework of the jet's morphology. This framework, which represents the fundamental structure of the jet, is coupled with a quantitative assessment of the interfaces' displacement or volume modification throughout the process, thereby facilitating the reconstruction of the original jet configuration. Furthermore, we evaluate several metrics to classify and differentiate the resulting frameworks. These measures encompass conventional parameters such as branch length distribution following their division into constituent parts, as well as a more advanced representation of the structure known as Topology Morphology Descriptor (TMD), which generates an equivalent representation of the structures by encoding the spatial topology into a concise format.

Researchers discovered that certain influenza viruses exhibit active movement on surfaces with carbohydrate layers by rolling along them, as shown in recent studies. This phenomenon was previously proposed to be an example of viral surface metabolism, where the collection of spike proteins interacts with the carbohydrates, generating mechanical movement through a self-organizing process. This research aims to investigate in greater detail the physical aspects underlying this rolling motion, developing a theory that explains the motor's behavior, as well as validating the results using simulations to analyze the impact of various factors. The outcomes of this study strongly indicate that viral movement on surfaces is statistically certain to occur when the virus exhibits enzymatic activity.

We examined over 8,000 massive, edge-on disk galaxies from the SDSS dataset, focusing on two types: S and U galaxies. Our analysis revealed that U galaxies have distinct characteristics, including bluer optical colors and higher star formation rates, compared to S galaxies. U galaxies, particularly those with more extreme warping, exhibited higher star formation rates. Contrary to expectations, U galaxies in groups and clusters do not show a correlation with the tidal force exerted by their nearest neighbor. However, U galaxies are more common in groups and clusters and share similarities with 'jellyfish' galaxies formed through ram-pressure stripping (RPS). This led us to suggest that RPS could be a potential mechanism explaining the presence of U galaxies in groups and clusters.

This research focuses on harmonic functions within the context of a particular type of manifold where the Ricci curvature decreases over time and the scalar curvature remains constant. We have derived a key theorem demonstrating that bounded harmonic functions are constant in this specific type of manifold, without relying on an established growth estimate. Consequently, this result implies that the set of all harmonic functions that grow at a polynomial rate on these manifolds is finite-dimensional.

Compounds composed of potassium ($A=$ K, Rb, Cs) combined with boron in a 2:1 ratio, exhibit unique cubic structures called the Laves phase with a specific Fd$\bar{3}$m symmetry. The arrangement of atoms within these crystals permits the existence of chirally behaving phonons, which correspond to atoms circling their equilibrium positions. Given that inversion symmetry and time reversal symmetry govern the total pseudo-angular momentum of the system, this momentum is zero. By introducing dopants, researchers find that this can result in a new crystal structure, F$\bar{4}3$m. Novel materials, KRbBi$_{4}$ and RbCsBi$_{4}$, exhibit no dynamic instability; the inversion symmetry disruption however, leads to phonons with a non-zero total pseudo-angular momentum. Chirally behaving phonons emerge at wave vectors located at the Brillouin zone boundary in both systems under consideration. By exploring this possibility of phonon engineering through spatiotemporal manipulation, researchers open the door to novel strategies for macroscopic angular momentum control.

In insulators, Born effective charges relate to how the positioning of individual atomic sublattices generates electric polarization, a concept seemingly unrelated to metals and doped semiconductors. However, our findings reveal that, when the conventional approximation is surpassed, nonadiabatic Born effective charges become well defined in metals within a specific frequency range. We also observe that, unlike in insulators, the summation of nonadiabatic Born effective charges from sublattices in metals does not equal zero but rather correlates directly with the Drude weight. These conclusions were verified through calculations using density functional perturbation theory, as applied to aluminum, and to a binary aluminum compound.

We are reassessing the significance of thermal fluctuations in incompressible fluid turbulence and determining their relevance on a particular scale. As earlier research by Betchov predicted decades ago, this scale is equivalent to the Kolmogorov length, although it's still many orders of magnitude greater than the average free path. This finding suggests that the non-random, or deterministic, form of the Navier-Stokes equation is insufficient for modeling the turbulence dissipation range within molecular fluids. Instead, the fluctuating hydrodynamics equation by Landau and Lifschitz provides a more accurate description within this range. Specifically, our analysis implies that the exponentially decaying energy spectrum and the extreme intermittency in the far-dissipation range of turbulence predicted by deterministic Navier-Stokes equations will generally be replaced by Gaussian thermal equipartition at scales below the Kolmogorov length. High-Reynolds-number behaviors are generally different from their low-Reynolds-number counterparts due to the interplay between the inertial range and the far-dissipation range, and this interplay can lead to various alternative behaviors such as the extreme and the extreme and the extreme and the extreme and the extreme and the extreme and the extreme.

Three-dimensional topological insulators can be identified by a magnetoelectric coefficient that is quantized in units of phi, however this coefficient becomes zero when time-reversal symmetry is present due to the inverse relationship between magnetoelectric and Aharonov-Bohm effects. We suggest an alternative method using a loop of wire to quantify the topological insulator's properties via the non-equilibrium distribution of charge current and electric potential within a probed region. This approach allows us to derive a unique quantum hall effect in which the current and voltage contact leads are influenced by the hall angle but also coupled with a spatial distribution that exploits the quasi-one-dimensional nature of the hall effect to distinguish between trivial and non-trivial states even when time-reversal symmetry is present.

In systems featuring delayed nonlinearity, we observe chaotic diffusion as a typical trait, where it is found that modulating the time delay periodically can significantly enhance diffusion, by expanding the area occupied by the system and its stability properties. This diffusion can be manipulated through various means, such as adjusting the amplitude and frequency of the modulation, and it exhibits complex and interdisciplinary connections, including linkages to stochastic resonance and quasiperiodically forced Mitchell-Yorke turbulence.

We provide rigorous definitions for sound and sufficient denotational and operational interpretations of the stochastic lambda calculus. By adapting established techniques to reason about high-level probabilistic code, this study achieves a breakthrough in linking operational and denotational views with a proven adequacy theorem, thereby closing a key outstanding issue identified in earlier work (Bacci et al., 2018).

Discussions among developers encompass a variety of interactions, including in-person conversations and online comments, which are beneficial to label as relevant to software design for documentation and improvement purposes. This is made possible through a process known as design mining, which applies machine learning to categorize discussions as pertaining to design. This paper showcases a simple model for design mining, revealing that current methods suffer from inconsistent conclusions on various discussion types and projects. We then introduce and demonstrate two effective techniques - data enrichment and project adaptation - that enhance design mining's reliability and adaptability across different datasets, achieving a satisfactory classification rate of 0.88 within a dataset and 0.80 across different datasets.

A proposed model explains the existence of gravity, dark energy, and dark matter.
Dark energy and dark matter stem from a false vacuum state's random energy fluctuations, characterized by large-scale negative and short-scale positive pressures, respectively, representing incoherent and coherent aspects of a superfluid/supersolid state.
Gravity emerges from topological defects within the post-inflation virtual "condensate" component.
Consequently, it is anticipated that exotic particles that could explain dark matter will not be detected at the LHC.
Moreover, it is suggested that the de Sitter horizon plays a role in holographic dark energy due to the restriction of the vacuum's degree of freedom based on the universe's age.
Finally, it is proposed that a more accurate theory of everything involves a "pre-inflation" phase where the universe undergoes "anti-inflation" before entering the radiation-dominated era.
In this scenario, the universe undergoes an infinite number of cycles, eventually leading to a metastable state, and a more accurate cosmological model could incorporate these phases to achieve a more accurate understanding of the universe's evolution.

Proximal methods can efficiently uncover the underlying pattern in nonsmooth optimization problems, and, in many cases, identifying this structure is a free byproduct, also enhancing the convergence rate once aligned with that of the problem's optimal solution. Nonetheless, pinpointing the exact structure is not possible without adaptation. By assuming a proximal gradient method is able to recognize the differentiability manifolds in a nonsmooth objective, we show that incorporating Riemannian Newton-like techniques alongside the proximal gradient steps results in a significantly improved convergence rate for specific nondegenerated nonsmooth nonconvex optimization problems. Moreover, our algorithm is accompanied by a numerical study that includes optimizations regulated by $\ell_1$-norm and trace-norm.

We are introducing a new concept called weakly $1$-absorbing prime ideals within a commutative ring with identity, which serves as an extension to the existing notion of weakly prime ideals. A prime ideal $I$ in a ring $R$ is said to be weakly $1$-absorbing if for every three non-unit elements $a,b,$ and $c$ in $R$ where their product is non-zero and within $I$, it follows that either the product of $a$ and $b$ is in $I$, or $c$ is in $I$. Our research presents numerous results regarding the characteristics and examples of weakly $1$-absorbing prime ideals. It has been proven that if $I$ is a weakly $1$-absorbing prime ideal in a ring $R$ where the product of three non-zero ideals is completely contained in $I$, it then holds that either the product of the first two ideals is completely contained in $I$, or the third ideal is completely contained in $I$. Additionally, it is demonstrated that if $I$ and $J$ are two ideals in a ring $R$ where their product is completely contained in a weakly $1$-absorbing prime ideal, then either the product of $I$ and $J$ is completely contained in this ideal, or one of $I$ or $J$ is completely contained in this ideal$.

We present new findings for two semileptonic decay processes, $B^0$ decaying into $\rho^-$ and a lepton-neutrino pair, and $B^+$ decaying into $\rho^0$ with the same pair, utilizing data from Belle II's sample equivalent to 189.9/fb, collected using the SuperKEKB $e^-e^+$ collider. To identify these decays, the research involved reconstructing the full recoil $B$-meson within hadronic $B$-decay products, due to a lack of lepton information. As a result, the researchers were able to establish a highly background-restricted environment in which to search for these rare $B$-decay reactions. Ultimately, the researchers computed total branching fraction estimates for these two decays: $B^0$ into $\rho^-$ and a lepton-neutrino pair, with a value of $(6.12\pm0.65\pm0.66\pm0.75)(10^{-5})$, and $B^+$ decaying into $\rho^0$ with the same pair, at $(7.8\pm2.1\pm1.3\pm1.4)(10^{-5})$, in conjunction with a comparison to theoretical predictions from the Standard Model and the SM's predicted estimates for these decays, which are $(5.5\pm1.5)\times 10^{-5}$ for

Our team employed photonic technology to revolutionize the conventional traditional spectroscopy used across science, engineering, and industry for decades. By incorporating a sample on a photonic chip alongside precise light control and highly sensitive detectors, spectral analysis becomes more streamlined, faster, and more sensitive. Furthermore, photonic devices leverage the conjunction of diverse physical light-matter interactions to offer distinct advantages over traditional methods. Nevertheless, the typical template-based photonic chip incorporates a single specific light interaction at a time, limiting its potential for comprehensive spectral analysis. To address this limitation, our work features a general-purpose photonic chip that integrates multiple light interactions into a unified platform, enabling concurrent processing of diverse optical signals. This allows for functions like multiplexed light coupling, coherent light combination, and on-chip spectral cross-correlation, thereby enhancing the performance of various spectroscopic techniques and pioneering a new era in photonic spectroscopy.

In the last few years, various machine learning models have emerged with the aim of tackling polypharmacy side effects, predicting medication interactions, and optimizing combination therapies. This paper takes a comprehensive approach, offering a theoretical framework that can address these challenges through relational machine learning models. It provides key concepts, assesses existing model architectures, discusses relevant evaluation metrics, datasets, and testing protocols. Furthermore, it highlights significant potential applications and suggests vital research paths for the future in this field.

Several local authorities face challenges in deploying advanced automated
evaluation of road damage due to a lack of necessary infrastructure, high costs,
and the requirements of specialized workforces for effective results. To overcome
these issues, we've developed a reliable RUD (Road, Camera, GPS, IMU) data
annotation tool. This tool facilitates the training of automated damage detection
models on existing data by allowing non-experts to accurately annotate data.
We've also introduced a method for the effective annotation of a substantial dataset
exceeding 10,000 images, achieving outstanding results with AUC scores of 0.97 for
crack detection and 0.94 for damage classification.

Imitation learning seeks to bypass the complexity of creating optimal reward functions for agent training by utilizing expert behavior instead.  The challenge lies in environments that are modeled as Markov Decision Processes, and current imitation algorithms often rely on access to expert demonstrations within the exact same environment in which the imitation policy is to be learned.  However, when discrepancies arise between expert and agent domains due to varying dynamics, perspectives, or morphologies, imitation tasks become increasingly difficult.  This paper proposes a new framework that establishes correspondences across disparate domains using only unaligned trajectories containing states from the expert domain.  The framework leverages cycle-consistency constraints in both the state space and a domain-agnostic latent space to facilitate this correspondence.  Additionally, it ensures temporal alignment using a normalized position estimator.  Once the correspondence is established, the learned demonstrations can be directly transferred and applied to the target domain, empowering imitation.  The approach is validated through experiments across a diverse range of complex domains.

A major uncertainty in determining the initial mass function of the first (Population III) stars hinges on the ultimate fate of secondary protostars that form in the accretion disk - whether they will merge or remain separate. We concentrate on how the initial star formation was influenced by magnetic effects in a cosmological setting with existing magnetic fields. We conducted a series of simulations of magnetohydrodynamics, running up to 1000 years following the initial protostar formation. To represent the protostars and their magnetic field structures, we utilized a stiff equation of state approach instead of the conventional sink particle technique. Ten years after the initial protostar formation, we observed an amplification in magnetic field strength from picogauss to kilogauss in the region around protostars, matching that of contemporary stars. Due to the rapid orbital rotations in the vicinity of protostars, their magnetic field became increasingly wound up over the initial decade of protostar formation. As mass accretion proceeded, the area where the magnetic field plays a crucial role in determining gas dynamics expands outward and prevents the disk from fragmenting at early stages. We discovered that the ultimate fate of secondary protostars is invariable - they all merge in a process stimulated by their magnetic field - due to the cosmological framework used in this study. The initial mass function of the first stars is thus invariable also, whereas variations in magnetic field amplification and cosmological framework can produce different mass functions.

Association rule analysis is a widely used technique in Data Mining. This method involves partial implications between binary variables, which can be constrained by parameters such as confidence and support levels. We delve into the concept of redundancy among association rules from a theoretical perspective. Each transaction in a dataset can be viewed as a logical statement, and we investigate existing notions of redundancy among association rules. We explore alternative definitions of redundancy and introduce new characterizations, highlighting relationships between these concepts. Moreover, we establish lower and upper bounds for the number of redundant rules in a dataset.

Individuals within the criminal justice system frequently suffer from mental health disorders.  An analysis of North Carolina court cases between 1999 and 2009 examined how court-ordered mental health treatment as part of probation affects an offender's chances of returning to the justice system.  The research focuses on offenders who were sentenced to probation and assesses those who were required to undergo mental health treatment against those who were not.  It discovered that receiving mental health treatment as part of their sentence lowered the odds of recidivism within a three-year time frame by 17 percent or 5.6 percentage points.  The data suggests mental health treatment reduces future violent and property crimes more significantly and that this reduction in crimes increases with time since the original conviction.  An economic analysis reveals each dollar spent on mental health treatment may yield a 3-to-1 return on investment due to reduced incarceration costs and savings from fewer crimes.

The authors of the paper delve into generalized Apostol-Bernoulli polynomials with parameters, derive their generating functions, examine key properties and relationships, and establish connections to other notable polynomials.

Radio maps are being explored as a promising approach to equip advanced wireless networks with situational awareness. They will likely serve a pivotal function in enabling UAV communications by allowing the assessment of signal strength and interference levels at unknown locations. Different from conventional radio map estimation techniques, which depend on uncontrolled sensor measurements, a new method proposes that a UAV collect data at designated locations along a carefully planned route to quickly obtain a reliable map. This route is optimized using a measure that identifies the most informative locations to collect data from. A novel real-time Bayesian algorithm has been created to constantly update the map estimate and the associated uncertainty metric with every new data point, allowing the process to take place in real-time.

This paper outlines a novel approach, GLA, for identifying unusual patterns in discrete time series by leveraging Hidden Markov Models and clustering techniques. At its core lies the comparison of sequential data segments. The process involves clustering time series segments, labeling them as either normal or anomalous based on their probability of occurring, and finally removing any detected anomalies. The performance of this method is evaluated using artificial data and real-world time series from the Twitter and Netflix streams, as well as network traffic data. The resulting case study highlights the potential of this method to automatically identify distinct sections within time series data.

This research delves into a multi-aspect approach to person verification incorporating auditory, visual, and thermal modalities. Given the efficacy of auditory and visual modality combination, this investigation extends to exploring the effect of incorporating thermal images on performance. Specifically, it demonstrates that a multi-aspect system surpasses its single-modal and bi-modal counterparts, achieving a 20% boost in accuracy over the former and matching the latter's results. Moreover, it shows that the integration of thermal images enhances model robustness against the manipulation of audio and visual elements.

Generating new training data through augmentation is achieved by appending existing examples to create new instances. We've found this approach to be both simple and cost-effective in boosting the performance of pre-optimized Transformer and Conformer models. Specifically, enhancements of up to 2.83 WER and 6.87 WER are seen in the LibriSpeech-960h test sets, and even higher when models were combined with fusion. Moreover, improvements of as much as 0.9 WER are recorded on the CoVoST-2 for several non-English languages following this training methodology. Notably, results indicate the magnitude of gain largely correlates with the size of initial training data. It is observed that our augmentation method can function effectively even when not utilizing speaker information. We've also demonstrated its effectiveness in translating spoken content into other languages by using similar test sets, revealing notable reductions in WER of as much as 7.65. Finally, comparable effects are observed on the speech emotion recognition task with decent reductions in F1-score.

Consider a parametric family of distributions defined by $f(y|\theta)$ where $\theta$ is a parameter from the set $\Omega$, a function $\eta(\theta)$ and an unknown distribution $G$ as the mixing distribution. It is necessary to estimate the expected value of $\eta(\theta)$ based on a mixing distribution, denoted as $\eta_G$, using independent observations of $Y_1,...,Y_n$ where each observation follows $f(y|\theta_i)$ and the associated parameters $\theta_i$ follow the distribution $G$ independently. This work delves into finding Generalized Maximum Likelihood Estimators (GMLE) to solve this estimation problem. Key properties and GMLE representations are explored and we discuss how a previous result from Kiefer and Wolfowitz (1956) can be applied to this context, including the scenario where the parameters $\theta_1,...,\theta_n$ are treated as fixed constants. Furthermore, we discuss how estimating $\eta_G$ is equivalent to the non-parametric empirical Bayes estimation method under squared loss. GMLE's utility in sampling problems is illustrated through simulated examples and real data analysis.

Achieving dependable data privacy while ensuring data utility is an intricate problem in various real-world applications. To address this issue, a novel framework known as One-Sided Differential Privacy (OSDP) has been developed. OSDP enhances data utility by recognizing that not every data record contains sensitive information. However, the previous approaches in this field made the assumption that data records were statistically independent. Inspired by occupancy data analysis in building management systems, the current research builds upon the one-sided differential privacy framework by accounting for inter-dependent data records. Furthermore, a statistical model is developed to estimate a data distributor's confidence in the sensitivity of individual data records. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed data publishing algorithm, which employs the confidence model, over prior approaches. Lastly, the study investigates the trade-offs between utility and cost associated with this confidence model.

In protoplanetary disks, it is not unusual to come across gas and dust emission substructures.
These substructures may have connections to the formation of planets themselves.
Our investigation into the AS 209 gas substructures employed thermochemical modeling using RAC2D and precise observations from the Molecules with ALMA at Planet-forming Scales project.
Our observations of C$^{18}$O J=2-1 revealed a distinct trough at 88 au that overlapped with the areas of several millimeter dust continuum emission gaps.
We observed that CO column density could be linked to surface-density fluctuations or chemical alterations, while C$_2$H column density was tied to changes in the C/O ratio rather than surface density changes in the gas.
However, our models require a particular set of conditions to replicate the observed structure - specifically, a particular level of CO depletion that isn't consistent with other features in the disk.
Alternative models that take into account the disk's gas accretion rate and CO abundance also failed to replicate the observation of a single CO hole.
A custom model that simulates the disk's gas accretuation is then proposed to explain the gas substructures in AS 209.

The analysis of time-stamped data is a fundamental aspect of scientific and industrial research, where the vast amount of generated data poses significant processing challenges due to increased resolution, input channels, and event acquisition rates. To overcome these obstacles, we've created the Extensible Time-tag Analyzer (ETA), an advanced, yet intuitive software solution that streamlines time-stamped data analysis and visualization. Leveraging an integrated approach of flowcharts and modular code snippets, our tool empowers users to perform in-depth data correlation and analysis, while maintaining high computational performance and efficiency.

We prove the existence of'mild solutions' for a mean field game involving first-order controls with a constraint requiring state and control trajectories remain within a closed, bounded Euclidean space area. This outcome builds upon Cannarsa and Capuani's research, which established the basis for these'mild solutions' in Cannarsa et al.'s (2021) study. In our research, we relax the initial conditions of Cannarsa and Capuani's (2020) existence proof for the mean field game's Hamiltonian system, while maintaining the existence of the mean field game's first-order Hamiltonian-Jacobi-Bellman equation's solution.

Recent analyses of Gaia data have led to the discovery of new stellar structures, a newly classified type known as stellar "strings". We conducted an in-depth examination of these structures, focusing on their spatial patterns, movement, chemical composition, and whether their members originated from a shared location. By analyzing the distribution of these structures in 3D space, we discovered that they do not exhibit improved spatial alignment as expected in real, interconnected structures, contrary to earlier assumptions. Calculating the masses of these structures based on their radial velocity dispersion revealed that they are actually not gravitationally bound. Furthermore, we found that these structures' ages, when compared to their actual age spread, appear excessively large. It is also worth noting that these structures, while seemingly homogeneous, can exhibit identical characteristics if composed of randomly selected stars from separate clusters, indicating that these structures might be mere coincidences. These results suggest that these structures are actually dispersed, isolated star groups rather than meaningful astrophysical entities.

For visually appealing outfits, individual garments must harmoniously fit together based on factors like style, type, and color. Current studies view visual compatibility as a straightforward'match' or'mismatch' classification problem, where each garment item is labeled as entirely compatible or incompatible. Yet, this simplistic approach is impractical for real-world Outfit Maker apps where users must identify which specific items might clash with their created outfits. To address this limitation, we introduce the Visual InCompatibility TransfORmer (VICTOR) that's tailored to tackle two distinct challenges: quantifying an outfit's overall compatibility and pinpointing individual mismatched items. Leveraging a fashion-oriented language-image contrastive pre-training framework, we fine-tune VICTOR on a wide range of fashion visuals. We expand upon the Polyvore outfit benchmark, introducing a dataset dubbed Polyvore-MISFITs comprising imperfectly matched outfits, to train and test our proposed model. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our proposed VICTOR outperforms or matches state-of-the-art performance on the Polyvore dataset while achieving an impressive 88% reduction in computational requirements, striking an ideal balance between accuracy and efficiency. We publicly release the VICTOR implementation at https://github.com/stevejpapad/Visual-InCompatibility-Transformer.

The framework of quantum resource theory has significantly advanced quantum physics, enabling the unification of diverse methods to quantify specific quantum effects. It plays a pivotal role in optimizing their utility across various applications. The incorporation of radical quantum phenomena such as coherence, entanglement, and nonclassicality has enabled their application in real-world contexts. The theoretical framework of quantum resource theory categorizes quantum states into 'free' and'resource' sets. Operations associated with free states emerge naturally from the system's constraints, whereas resource theories aim to discover and harness the potential within the restricted set. Recent breakthroughs in the field of standard harmonic oscillator quantum states have sparked rapid growth and advancements in the generalized quantum optical framework. The incorporation of contemporary ideas such as nonlinearity, non-Hermitian theories, and $q$-deformed bosonic systems aims to expand the scope of quantum resource theory even further. This article reviews recent developments in the resource theories of generalized quantum optical states and their applications.

As the number of devices contributing to cross-device federated learning grows, synchronizing updates can significantly reduce efficiency. The FedBuff algorithm mitigates this limitation by enabling asynchronous updates and securely aggregated data sharing, thus improving scalability while protecting user privacy. Building on the FedBuff framework for asynchronous learning, this study enhances existing research by relaxing the requirement that the gradient magnitude must remain within predefined bounds. Theoretical convergence rate analysis of the modified FedBuff algorithm considers factors like diverse data sets, varying batch sizes, and delay intervals.

This study introduces a functional calculus tailored to a countable set of operators generating contraction strongly continuous semigroups. We select polynomial tempered distributions as the symbol class for this calculus. We then establish a key differential property and elucidate its mapping in relation to the commutant of a polynomial shift semigroup. As a concrete demonstration of its utility, we examine the function of a countable set of second derivative operators.

Recent research suggests combining the Swampland program with dark energy's scarcity could predict the presence of an additional dimension with a characteristic scale of a micron. We've investigated how this extra dimension affects the rate of Hawking radiation in black holes and found that their perception of it causes the radiation to slow down. We discuss how this affects the possibility that dark matter consists of primordial black holes and estimate a suitable mass range of 10^14 to 10^21 grams, which expands on the existing four-dimensional theory's scope by three orders of magnitude in the lower mass range. Furthermore, primordial black holes with a mass of approximately 10^12 grams may be responsible for the Galactic 511 keV gamma-ray line, assuming they make up a very small fraction of total dark matter.

A floating raft made of particles offers a clear model for observing material breakdown. Due to the slow timescales, both the large-scale expansion of the raft and the particle movement can be easily examined. The breakdown of the raft occurs in two stages: first, the particles detach from the rapidly expanding substrate, and second, the displaced particles cluster together, forming compact aggregates. To understand the large-scale behavior, we simulated the raft breakdown using a model that accounts for the drag experienced by the particles, and found that the results align with previous experiments. The simulation revealed that the breakdown pattern is determined by the balance between the expansion rate of the substrate and the buoyancy force acting on the particles. A slower substrate expansion results in a more irregular breakdown pattern compared to a rapid expansion. The optimization of the raft's stress through shape adjustments also plays a crucial role in determining the breakdown pattern. Depending on the drag experienced by the particles, the time it takes for the raft to break down can differ significantly.

The main challenge hindering the advancement of integrated gallium nitride electronics lies in its low hole mobility. In our investigation, we consider whether the mobility can be enhanced through epitaxial matching of GaN to certain II-IV nitride materials. We performed detailed computations utilizing the ab initio Boltzmann transport equation to calculate the hole mobility of GaN, revealing that aligning GaN under uniaxial compressive strain by matching it to ZnGeN$_2$ or MgSiN$_2$ inorganic materials flips the order of the heavy and light hole bands, resulting in a reduced hole mass along the compression axis. Consequently, our calculations indicate that matching GaN to ZnGeN$_2$ or MgSiN$_2$ boosts its room temperature hole mobility by 50% and 260%, respectively, when compared to strain-free GaN. Furthermore, our study on the strain-mobility trends discloses a nonlinear correlation. Moreover, our model suggests that matching GaN to an imaginary solid solution composed of Zn$_{0.75}$Ge$_{0.75}$Mg$_{0.25}$Si$_{0.25}$N$_2$ could increase its hole mobility by 160%.

Our novel TD learning approach overcomes a key limitation of traditional TD-lambda by bypassing the need to maintain a vast experience buffer, making it practical for robots to learn complex tasks in real-world settings. By integrating Gaussian Process regression, our algorithm enables the robot to selectively sample only the most crucial experiences from its environment, thereby allowing for simultaneous exploration and efficient use of computational resources. Empirical evidence demonstrates that our approach yields comparable performance to state-of-the-art deep reinforcement learning methods in challenging underwater navigation tasks, showcasing its practicality and effectiveness for robots navigating complex environments.

We examine isothermic surfaces with a Hopf differential that decomposes into a real function and a specific quadratic differential with a singular point. However, this differential is nonzero and holomorphic throughout the rest of the surface except at this singular point. By focusing on a patch excluding the singular point, we find new isothermic surfaces applying the Darboux and Calapso transformations. Furthermore, we investigate how the transformed patches behave as they approach the singular point and check for continuity in that region.

We analyze the statistical approximation of the $L^2$-operator defined as $[Pf](x) = \mathbb{E}[f(Y) | X = x]$ given the joint distribution of $X$ and $Y$ on a certain topological space under the assumption that the expectation is relatively independent of $X's$ marginal distribution. We modify the operator to depend only on $X's$ marginal distribution and demonstrate that this modification is of Hilbert-Schmidt rank for certain distributions, which allows for efficient statistical estimation. We also establish that maximizing the estimated expected output or using regularization techniques can yield consistent estimators of the operator. In the context of conditional independence testing, this operator corresponds to the conditional covariance operator and our results reconcile the hypotheses of that test with properties of this operator. We further provide a simulation study to illustrate our findings and prove that our statistical estimates converge at a rate that is based on the operator's smoothness, not the sample size.

This paper builds upon recent studies by Kim-Kim on the $\lambda$-analogues of $r$-Stirling numbers of the first kind. We explore and define the $\lambda$-analogues of $r$-Stirling numbers of the second kind and their associated properties. We derive recurrence relations, identities and present comparable results for $\lambda$-analogues of Whitney-type $r$-Stirling numbers of the second kind.

The consideration of temporal contexts within knowledge graph embeddings presents a chance for enhanced performance in related tasks. Nevertheless, current models have a unified fact representation that fails to distinguish the significance of time, which might lead to confusion in temporal relationships. To address this limitation, this study proposes the Temporal Entity Embedding (TEE) model, whose entity representations are sensitive to time by combining past and future temporal information with individual fact embeddings. TEE was tested using the FB15K237 and WN18RR datasets, and the results indicate that it surpasses existing methods in entity classification and link prediction tasks.

This note enhances and reinforces Bates' theorem which indicates that for row-finite graphs classified as strong shift equivalent, their associated graph C*-algebras are also Morita equivalent. This discovery opens up possibilities to investigate if the stronger notion of Morita equivalence effectively describes strong shift equivalence. This line of inquiry will likely hold significant value for ongoing research regarding infinite graphs and their associated C*-algebras. Moreover, this note specifically explores insplits and outsplits as key examples of strong shift equivalences, demonstrating that these equivalences lead to Morita equivalences that maintain consistency across various weighted gauge actions. Consequently, a question is raised about whether strong shift equivalence can be expressed as a product of insplits and outsplits.

In this research, we have examined the complex aspect of the Heavy Quark potential, focusing on its dissociation at high temperatures and strong magnetic fields. Our work builds upon previous studies by introducing three distinct spatial gauge choices, which leads to novel findings. Notably, at high magnetic fields, the heavy quark potential exhibits a unique Z2 symmetry breaking, differing from its Higgs-like transition characteristics in the absence of a magnetic field. Furthermore, we have mapped the heavy quark potential's dissociation mechanisms in various gauge choices and discovered that certain features remain intact despite changes in the ground state characteristics.

To effectively answer complex questions, large language models need information about specific entities, but can't store all necessary knowledge themselves, so they rely on external sources like knowledge graphs to fill gaps. Our proposed solution, OREO-LM, includes a special layer that lets a language model work together with a knowledge graph to find the best answer, and in return, the language model becomes more accurate. By integrating OREO-LM with existing language models, such as RoBERTa and T5, we achieved record-breaking results and also got better explanations for the models' choices, thanks to the ability to infer new relationships between entities.

We have developed a novel method of constructing high dimensional expanders by utilizing covering spaces of simplicial complexes. Building upon expander graphs, high dimensional expanders play a vital role in theoretical computer science but unfortunately, there are only a few constructions available that offer arbitrarily small local spectral expansion.

Our research involves presenting a probabilistic algorithm that takes an arbitrary high dimensional complex as input and generates a sub-complex through a series of random removals of simplices. The algorithm creates an expander by removing simplices that have minimal local expansion. The created expander possesses a spectral expansion of at least an arbitrary factor, and the algorithm also ensures that the new expander retains the topological structure of the original complex.

Furthermore, we have discovered an independent method of creating high dimensional expanders by using covering spaces of simplicial complexes. The method involves breaking down the complex into sub-complexes based on a specific metric and then applying a topological version of the expander mixing time concept. The new metric preserves the structural characteristics of the original complex and offers a better local expansion due to its construction.

Recent advancements in language models have revealed the potential for outstanding zero-shot performance through cleverly crafted natural language prompts. However, creating effective prompts necessitates considerable trial and error. Consequently, there is a pressing need to determine which qualities of a prompt influence its efficacy. To this end, we have collected and standardized a diverse set of prompts designed for specific tasks and tested them on tasks for which they were not originally intended. Our quantitative analysis across multiple fixed choice datasets demonstrates that prompts containing answer options and those not utilized during pre-training exhibit notable performance enhancements.

We have computed the Benois $\mathscr{L}$-invariants for weight one cuspforms and their corresponding adjoint representations. Furthermore, our calculations extend Gross' $p$-adic regulator to non-critical Artin motives, which aligns with Deligne's framework. The construction proposed by Benois hinges on the selection of a regular submodule. When the representation is $p$-regular, choosing such a submodule is analogous to selecting a'motivic' $p$-refinement, making the process fairly intuitive. However, when the representation is $p$-irregular, things become more intricate as regular submodules are categorized by a flag variety, resulting in an abundance of choices that involve continuous parameters. Despite these complications, our analysis in select examples highlights how Hida theory and eigencurve geometry can facilitate the identification of a limited set of choices that possess notable arithmetic and'mixed-motivic' significance.

Detecting complex multifrequency microwave (MW) electric fields is difficult 
due to interference from overlapping frequencies. Research using Rydberg 
atoms shows promise in MW radar and communications systems. Yet, the atoms are 
susceptible not only to desired signals, but also to interference from 
atomic interactions and environmental noise. To resolve these challenges, we've 
successfully integrated Rydberg atoms with deep learning algorithms, allowing the 
model to leverage the atoms' sensitivity while minimizing the impact of noise 
without requiring the resolution of complex mathematical equations. In a key 
test, our Rydberg-deep learning system has enabled the direct extraction of 
embedded information from frequency-locked signals, marking a significant 
advancement in the technology.

UGC 8839, an exceptionally faint spiral galaxy, is characterized by minimal star formation except in a substantial HII region located in the extreme outer rim of its disk. A comparative study with four similar spiral galaxies reveals that the unusual star formation in UGC 8839 is likely attributed to a highly stable, dark matter-dominated disk. Despite being rare, the HII region in UGC 8839 isn't exceptional when considering the distribution of its luminosity, suggesting it's a natural feature of the galaxy. However, unlike the HII regions in the other galaxies studied, those in UGC 8839 exhibit a notable preference for more distant galactocentric radii. The unique dynamics of UGC 8839 provide an opportunity to investigate how its baryonic matter affects its overall behavior, potentially leading to a better comprehension of its evolution.

For a quasiregular self-map in 3D space, research has demonstrated that the Hausdorff dimension of its fast escaping set can be any value within the range of 1 to 3. An estimated lower bound has also been proposed for the Hausdorff dimension of its Julia set under a specific growth constraint.

Using the Neutral Gas Ion Mass Spectrometer on board the Mars Atmospheric and Volatile Evolution/NASA Mars Science Laboratory mission, the oscillating CO$_{2}$ density in the upper Martian atmosphere, spanning between 120 and 190~km in altitude, is monitored. This observation sheds light on the effects of gravity waves (GWs), allowing scientists to analyze the behavior of GWs in the upper atmosphere under isothermal conditions and understand the role that the atmospheric background temperature plays in the propagation of GWs. Data obtained from past missions including the Mars Global Surveyor, the Mars Odyssey, and the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, in combination with the new MAVEN findings, reveal correlations between GW-induced density disturbances and the atmospheric background temperature, primarily found in the ODY mission's data collected over polar regions, rather than in the MGS and MRO datasets. Conversely, MRO's observations of the upper Martian atmosphere's behavior following the dust storms show an increased intensity of GWs compared to the pre-storm conditions.

The LHC holds the record for the highest energy particle collisions, encompassing not only proton-proton and heavy ion interactions but also those of photons with photons and hadrons. This capability stems from the fact that protons and ions within the LHC possess an electromagnetic field, acting as a source of photons, which can then interact either with other photons or with hadrons. Specifically, ultra-peripheral collisions occur when high-energy ions surpass the range of the strong force, enabled by virtual photons exchanged between the nuclei, whose numbers directly correlate with nuclear electric charge. Given its exceptional energy levels, the LHC serves as the most powerful photon source ever constructed, particularly in favouring photoproduction of heavy vector mesons due to their inherent affinity to photons. Recent experiments examining the forward J/psi production in lead-lead ultra-peripheral collisions at 5.02 TeV using the ALICE detector are featured.

Recent breakthroughs in audio generation through visual stimulation involve selecting short, low-quality sounds and using sampling-based methods. However, current models using top-notch graphics processing units can still take several minutes to sample one second of audio. Our approach presents a unified model able to produce visually relevant high-fidelity sounds and generate these in real-time. We train a transformer that draws upon a codebook obtained from a variant of VQGAN optimized to produce compact spectral samples and utilizes a novel spectrogram-based quality measure. These spectral samples are transformed into waveforms using a window-based generator, and our model's relevance is assessed using a novel PESAGN score. It outperforms previous audio generation research in both quality and similarity to the original clip.

Recurrent neural networks have emerged as highly effective algorithms for processing sequential data, including natural languages, sounds, and time-series information. In contrast to conventional feed-forward networks, they incorporate a self-referential mechanism, allowing for the retention of temporal context and the sequential transmission of information. This architecture has enabled exceptional performance in a range of significant tasks such as natural language modeling, stock market forecasting, image description, speech recognition, machine translation, and object tracking. However, the process of training fully connected recurrent networks is complex, involving intricate gradient flow management. To address these challenges, numerous studies have been conducted. This article aims to provide an overview of recurrent neurons, their variations, and expert tips for efficiently training fully recurrent neural networks, drawing from the Multiple Object Tracking module within our IPO studio software.

Achieving a balance between pandemic control and economic considerations is a delicate task, as modeling under specific economic assumptions often yields non-transferable results. This research investigates how implementing timely moderate measures can resolve the trade-off between medical efficacy and economic impact, and attributes this finding to the broader concept of 'economic irreversibility,' illustrating its analogy to the principles of thermodynamics. A fundamental inequality provides a framework for the implementation of such measures. A novel theoretical approach underlying this methodology contributes to the body of econophysics research.

The development of modern machine learning applications is undergoing a transformation due to the growing use of AI. Advanced AI techniques are being employed to create high-quality data labeling. A novel approach to training machine learning models in collaboration with human labelers involves using a micro-tasks framework. When working on these tasks, each label is influenced by multiple, distinct factors including data information, opposing tasks, and the instructions provided to labelers. A new method for estimating the contribution of these factors on individual tasks has been created to facilitate efficient distribution of work. This system enables a 2.5 to 6.3 times decrease in the number of tasks required to train models, when compared to a random assignment method. Furthermore, the estimates reveal the significant role that instructions provided to labelers play in the training process and highlight a need for more effective instructions.

This work reveals underlying relationships between various, seemingly unrelated branches of mathematics: combinatorics, algebraic statistics, topology, and enumerative algebraic geometry. We emphasize discrete invariants, which have strong ties to the concept of Lorentzian polynomials. A common thread among these fields lies in a linear space of matrices.

This study provides an in-depth examination of how high pressure influences the anomalous Hall effect in Mn$_3$Sn, an antiferromagnetic compound with a triangular structure. Theoretical models predict that when exposed to pressure, Mn$_3$Sn undergoes a significant transformation, where the distances between certain atoms in the material's lattice undergo significant changes, potentially activating a new Hall effect that is not influenced by pressure. The experiment involved applying pressures of up to 2.2 GPa using a diamond anvil cell and conducted X-ray diffraction experiments to analyze the material's lattice structure at pressures exceeding 0.5 GPa, where the material experiences a phase transition. The results reveal that this phase transition enables the anomalous Hall effect at pressures above 0.5 GPa, where the material's Hall resistance shows a clear spike, particularly in the (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) atomic location, consistent with theoretical predictions. The experiment also discovered that the Hall effect in Mn$_3$Sn is not influenced by spin-orbit coupling and is likely driven by a new atomic mechanism that is supported by the material's lattice structure.

Formal knowledge acquisition is pivotal for developing artificial intelligence (AI)
capable of human-level cognition, with semantic relationships between entities being
one essential aspect of it. In the realm of Natural Language Processing (NLP), Relation
Extraction (RE), a subset of information extraction, plays a crucial role in acquiring
this vital knowledge automatically from natural language texts. By automatically
identifying semantic relationships between entities, RE contributes significantly to the
domain. Notably, recent studies have established Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) as the
prevalent approach for RE. In particular, the reliability of DNNs in the forms of
supervised and distant supervision methods makes them highly sought-after solutions
for RE. This article serves as an introduction, offering an in-depth analysis of DNNs in
RE from two primary angles: supervised RE and distant supervision RE. It also covers
the emergence of new approaches, recent trends, and prospective avenues for further
research in the area of RE.

This study investigates a Steklov-Robin eigenvalue problem for the Laplacian in a particular class of annular domains. Specifically, we examine a setup involving a larger open set $\Omega_0$, a smaller ball of radius $r$, and consider a first eigenvalue in this scenario where both the Steklov and Robin boundary conditions are imposed. We then analyze the main features of the eigenvalue and its associated eigenfunctions, as well as how the eigenvalue changes when the domain parameters are modified.

We investigate a widespread challenge in analyzing complex graph systems: many real-world networks are more effectively modeled as hypergraphs, yet their associated datasets are often presented as projected graphs. To better comprehend this phenomenon, we establish a theoretical framework to examine its underlying principles and worst-case scenarios. This framework informs our proposal of supervised hypergraph reconstruction, a novel task aimed at recovering a real-world hypergraph from its graph projection using domain-specific knowledge. To achieve this, we develop a method that involves two components: first, a sampling strategy is employed to significantly reduce the large number of potential hyperedges; second, a hyperedge classifier with two optimized variants is designed to identify candidate hyperedges based on their structural significance in the graph. Our experiments validate the efficacy of our approach and reveal the superiority of our sampling technique over existing methods.
